📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, zenless Zone Zero brought some hot new information and a first look at its next major faction as part of The Game Awards 2025 ceremony. As part of the showcase, we got a glimpse of Ye Shunguang and Zhao - two upcoming Agents.

The segment also teased the new Angels of Delusion faction, though details on that are slim.

The gameplay reveal for Ye Shunguang and Zhao was very much the highlight of what was ultimately a smaller segment. Ye Shunguang is Zenless Zone Zero’s first dual-form Agent. She’s a Void Hunter who hails from Yunkui Summit.

Shunguang is a master swordswoman, and she can shift between two different forms. Her combat looks smooth and stylish, with a lot of aerial attacks and fast sword play. Zhao should be familiar to anyone who plays ZZZ. The rabbit Thiren has a bit of a slippery playstyle, rapidly weaving across the battlefield to deliver attacks with her greataxe.

Industry observers note that before the trailer ends, we get the Angels of Delusion teaser, which didn’t offer much, but it’s certainly something for us to look forward to in the new year. In case you missed it, Zenless Zone Zero’s latest revision - Version 2.4 - is live, having arrived over two weeks ago.

As ever, make sure to check out our updated Zenless Zone Zero codes if you plan to jump in over the next few weeks. Presently, ZZZ V2.4 is expected to run on a slightly truncated five-week schedule, with Version 2.5 now anticipated on December 30.

The Electric Baby Land Rover Defender And Range Rover GT Will Begin Production Next Year

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (524 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • JLR's all-electric baby Defender is coming soon.
  • In a recent development, while JLR didn't give much info on what the electric baby Defender will be, we do know that it will be built on the same Electrified Modular Architecture (EMA) platform that underpins the Range Rover GT.
  • Despite both cars being built in the same factory, Balaji seemed to suggest that only the Defender will go into production in 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

JLR's all-electric baby Defender is coming soon. According to Car and Driver, JLR boss PB Balaji recently remarked on an earnings call that the smaller, all-electric Defender will go into production at the end next year, alongside the upcoming Range Rover GT. There's no official name for the bite-sized Defender, but Balaji reportedly didn't want to call it the Defender Sport.

In a recent development, while JLR didn't give much info on what the electric baby Defender will be, we do know that it will be built on the same Electrified Modular Architecture (EMA) platform that underpins the Range Rover GT. So it makes sense that it'll be built at the same factory. That factory currently builds the existing piston-powered Discovery Sport and the Range Rover Evoque. So JLR is basically just replacing the current combustion cars with their upcoming electric counterparts.

Despite both cars being built in the same factory, Balaji seemed to suggest that only the Defender will go into production in 2027. There's not much word on any technical specs just yet, but EMA supports 800-volt architectures and is capable of housing both pure battery-electric powertrains and hybrids. The baby Defender could very well offer both, but whichever powertrain it has, it'll need to be capable off-road to deliver on its name.

According to Motor1, Mark Cameron, managing director of Defender and Discovery brands, mentioned "We have got to make sure everything we do as Defender has the DNA of the brand: epic built-to-last, go-anywhere capability.".

Pricing, specs, and range are all still under wraps, although it might make sense for either fresh electric product to have the same 118.5-kWh battery as the current Range Rover Electric. With it, the electric Rover is capable of 333 miles of range, and that uses a conventional platform. The battery is also capable of 350 kW DC fast-charging, which would be very competitive in the segment, so it might make sense for JLR to roll with that battery tech. The significant Range Rover Electric has a dual-motor powertrain, with 542 horsepower, but that might be a bit much for a baby Defender. Although, there could be a go-fast version with that much power, similar to the current Defender Octa.

Recent findings suggest that land Rover pushed the current full-size Defender's electric replacement out to sometime in the 2030s, so there shouldn't be any confusion between the full-size and bite-size models. If production begins in late 2027, that means we could see the baby Defender soon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Woodland version is bigger and more powerful than the standard Toyota bZ, and it may be a better deal right now.

Toyota now sells three electric SUVs in the US (see which one is the best fit for you): the bZ (previously called the bZ4Z), C-HR, and bZ Woodland.

The C-HR is a smaller, sportier crossover SUV, while the bZ Woodland adds a larger, more rugged option.

Toyota is presently offering a deal on the 2026 bZ Woodland for Black Friday that might be worth a look.

In a recent development, the deal includes 0% APR financing for 72 months, plus an extra $1,000 Holiday Bonus Cash. Toyota remarked that if you finance a newly introduced 2026 bZ Woodland for 72 payments, it will cost $13.89 for every $1,000 financed.

In comparison, the standard 2026 bZ is available with 1.99% interest for 72 months at $14.75 for every $1,000 financed.

For leasing, the standard 2026 Toyota bZ is cheaper, starting at $369 per month. The deal is for a 36-month lease with $4,369 due at signing for an effective cost of $490 per month.

However, that’s for the single-motor FWD version. Upgrading to AWD will cost around $606 a month for the same 36-month lease with $4,369 due at signing.

It has been revealed that toyota is promoting 2026 bZ Woodland leases as low as $449 a month. That’s also for a 36-month lease with $4,448 due at signing.

The Toyota bZ Woodland comes standard with a dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain, delivering a combined 375 horsepower, which is 37 hp more than the standard bZ SUV with AWD.

Industry observers note that toyota’s standard bZ is offered with FWD and AWD powertrains. FWD models deliver either 165 hp (XLE FWD) or 221 hp (XLE FWD Plus and Limited FWD), while AWD models produce a combined 338 hp.

The Woodland model is also 6″ longer than the standard bZ, opening up an additional 30 cubic feet of cargo space on the inside.

Toyota’s bigger SUV also adds a rugged look and off-road capabilities with 8.3″ of ground clearance and up to 3,500 lbs of towing capacity.

Other rugged upgrades are standard, including All-Terrain tires, black side molding, roof rails, and black wheel arch cladding.

Inside, both come with a 7″ digital cluster and a large 14″ touchscreen running the latest Toyota Audio Multimedia system with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

Industry observers note that although it uses the same 74.7-kWh battery as the standard bZ, the Woodland version offers slightly less driving range because of the added power and off-road equipment. The 2027 bZ Woodland has an estimated range of up to 281 miles with all-season tires, or 260 miles with the optional all-terrain tires.

Industry observers note that in comparison, the bZ is available with two battery packs: 57.7 kWh and 74.7 kWh. The base XLE FWD uses the 57.7 kWh battery, while the XLE AWD and FWD Plus, Limited AWD, and FWD models use the 74.7 kWh battery.

The standard 57.7 kWh battery provides an EPA range of up to 236 miles, while the 74.7 kWh battery provides up to 314 miles for FWD and 288 miles for AWD.

Recent findings suggest that both the bZ and bZ Woodland have a native NACS port, so drivers can use Tesla Superchargers without a separate adapter. It takes around 30 minutes to charge the battery from 10% to 80%.

The 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland is available in Base and Premium trims, starting at $45,380, or over $10,000 more than the standard bZ.

International Auto Theft Ring Busted in Canada, Cops Say, 96 Stolen Vehicles Worth $3 Million Recovered En Route to Africa

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (314 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that police in Canada say they have busted an organized auto theft crime ring that was stealing cars from the Great White North and shipping them across the ocean to Africa.
  • While the charges and announcement came on Monday, authorities have been putting this case together since March, when officers of the Peel Regional Police in Ontario put together what they called “Project Cadetta” in partnership with the Canada Border Services Agency.
  • Sources indicate that authorities say that many of these cars would get different VIN numbers as a part of the scheme.

Industry observers note that police in Canada say they have busted an organized auto theft crime ring that was stealing cars from the Great White North and shipping them across the ocean to Africa. Authorities declared a total of over 200 charges against 12 arrested individuals associated with the crime. In addition, officers recovered more than 90 vehicles worth a combined $4.5 million Canadian—$3.15 million in U.S. dollars.

While the charges and announcement came on Monday, authorities have been putting this case together since March, when officers of the Peel Regional Police in Ontario put together what they called “Project Cadetta” in partnership with the Canada Border Services Agency. Together, they initially focused on a single warehouse in Brampton, which allegedly was the staging area for stolen cars that were destined for West Africa via Canadian shipping ports. As police investigated the space, they began linking individuals to other locations.

Sources indicate that authorities say that many of these cars would get different VIN numbers as a part of the scheme. While they didn't detail the vehicles in question, they did show photos of a few; among them are several Lexus vehicles, a Land Rover Range Rover Sport, a Toyota Land Cruiser, and a BMW XM.

If this sounds familar, it’s not just you; this year alone, we at Road & Track have reported on similar theft rings several times. In April, authorities in the U.S. charged six people with being part of an illegal operation to steal cars and ship them to Africa. Police linked the suspects to some 130 cars. Then, later in the same month, police in New York said they found 72 more cars destined for West Africa. The cars in question included a Rolls-Royce, several BMWs, and an Audi SQ8. In May, Canadian police found another 40 stolen cars involved with a similar theft ring.

It has been revealed that the Game Awards 2025 ceremony brought us yet more gacha game news, this time a big announcement for Arknights: Endfield. The free-to-play game set in the the universe of Arknights has been in various forms of closed tests for a while, but it finally has a release date.

The game is set to arrive simultaneously across PC, PS5, and mobile (iOS, Android) on January 22, and pre-registrations continue to be open.

Gryphline broke the news on The Game Awards stage alongside a chunky trailer featuring a latest OneRepublic song. It actually ends up being a nice tone piece for the world of Arknights, showing a lot of cinematics alongside the music itself.

The developer-publisher also declared that so far, Arknights: Endfield has had over 30 million pre-registrations worldwide since pre-registrations went live. Some players have been able to play early, of course, with the most recent opportunity being Beta Test 2.

Sources indicate that if you’ve been following the game’s development, you’ll know that it was pretty clear we’re closer than ever to the official launch. The most recent beta build showed off polished content, with new animations and cutscenes.

We’ve been playing it ourselves, and we think you’re going to agree with our Arknights: Endfield character tier list. You can expect more coverage from us as we get closer to launch, and when the game actually arrives.

Though it might seem like it came out of nowhere, the game is based on the Arknights universe, itself a massive mobile game with over 100 million downloads. Endfield brings a different flavour to that world, with a mix of strategy, exploration and real-time combat, not unlike the many games created by HoYoverse.

You can pre-register yourself on the official website.

In a recent development, combining the lavish interior accommodations customary of a significant-body BMW with the firepower expected from the brand's legendary Motorsport division, the BMW XM is a seismically powerful plug-in hybrid SUV with a split personality. On the luxury side of the equation, the XM treats its occupants to a comfortable and spacious interior that is richly adorned with Merino leather and brushed aluminum. Rear-seat passengers even get throw pillows on their headrests.

But when it comes to performance, things get tricky. While a 738-hp plug-in-hybrid powertrain hidden behind the XM's overwrought snout helps rocket the super SUV to 60 mph in a claimed 3.6 seconds, the XM lacks the cornering finesse expected of M-badged models. Other hotted-up SIUVs, such as the Mercedes-AMG GLS-Class and BMW's own X7 M60i, meld luxury and performance more deftly.

Expert Tip: While it doesn’t pack the outright power of the XM Label, the BMW X7 M60i is a thoroughly extravagant 523-hp brute that adds utility with third-row seating. It's also around $45,000 less expensive than the XM.

Compare the 2027 BMW XM with the top vehicles in this segment with our upcoming compare tool.

We don't expect to see any changes to the BMW XM Label for the 2027 model year.

According to recent reports, if this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying newly introduced.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Following a series of high-profile food recalls and outbreaks this year, many Americans may be concerned about keeping their families safe from foodborne illness during the holidays.
  • In fact, according to a recent national survey by Orlando Health, around 60% of U.S.
  • Although several major foodborne illness outbreaks have ended and their associated recalls are no longer active, food safety remains an notable concern.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following a series of high-profile food recalls and outbreaks this year, many Americans may be concerned about keeping their families safe from foodborne illness during the holidays.

In fact, according to a recent national survey by Orlando Health, around 60% of U.S. adults say they’re more concerned about foodborne illness this year than in previous years.

Although several major foodborne illness outbreaks have ended and their associated recalls are no longer active, food safety remains an notable concern. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) estimates that 48 million people in the United States experience foodborne illness each year.

However, there are simple steps you can take to reduce the risk of foodborne illness when preparing holiday meals and storing leftovers.

While there were several food recalls in the United States over the summer, two of the largest involved Salmonella linked to jalapeños and Cyclospora linked to lettuce.

These outbreaks prompted widespread recalls and raised concerns about the safety of certain foods, particularly fresh produce.

Although health officials have since declared the major outbreaks over, some consumers may still be hesitant to purchase foods associated with previous recalls.

Even with this declaration, you may still feel nervous about purchasing certain foods, but experts say you don’t need to worry.

“Here in the United States, we have the safest food supply in the world. The recent recalls show that our food safety system is working,” said William Schaffner, MD, Professor, Division of Infectious Diseases at Vanderbilt University.

Michelle Routhenstein, preventive cardiology dietitian at Entirely Nourished, told Healthline that past recalls do not mean entire food categories need to be avoided. The key thing is whether the specific product you have matches a current recall, based on details such as brand, lot number, package size, and expiration date.

According to recent reports, “You should enjoy familiar foods, including properly cooked poultry, washed fruits and vegetables, and pasteurized dairy products,” she said. “The key is checking relevant recalls and practicing safe food handling.”.

“Before shopping or cooking, review FDA and USDA (U.S. Department of Agriculture) recall information and compare any relevant notices with the labels on your ingredients,” said Routhenstein.

Check the pantry and freezer, too: something purchased months ago may still be affected.

According to recent reports, “Stay alert to any news reports about food recalls and use good food preparation practices. Those simple actions should keep your holidays happy and safe,” said Schaffner.

Schaffner emphasized the importance of following safe food-handling practices when preparing everyday meals and holiday gatherings.

“Remember the longstanding advice: keep food hot or cold. Avoid long times at room temperature,” he noted.

Routhenstein advised focusing on four basics: clean, separate, cook, and chill.

It has been revealed that schaffner noted the importance of refrigerating leftovers promptly rather than leaving them at room temperature for extended periods. He recommends clearing the table and refrigerating leftovers soon after the meal ends.

Routhenstein reiterated that you should refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours rather than leaving them out to cool.

Divide turkey into smaller portions and transfer sides and gravy into shallow containers to help them cool rapidly, she advised.

Leftovers can typically be stored in the refrigerator for 3–4 days. If you don’t plan to eat them within that time, consider freezing them.

The notable thing is to keep an eye out for any new recalls, practice food safety, and enjoy your holiday meals!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Volkswagen’s revived Scout brand finally has vehicles coming off the line in South Carolina, but they’re validation units, not customer cars.
  • That’s two years later than the 2026 production start the manufacturer was talking about before it even broke ground on its $2 billion factory.
  • According to Scout’s announcement dated November 12, construction at the Production Center north of Columbia is in its final phase and most of the manufacturing equipment is installed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Volkswagen’s revived Scout brand finally has vehicles coming off the line in South Carolina, but they’re validation units, not customer cars. Scout confirms the first deliveries of the Traveler SUV and Terra pickup won’t happen until 2028.

That’s two years later than the 2026 production start the manufacturer was talking about before it even broke ground on its $2 billion factory.

According to Scout’s announcement dated November 12, construction at the Production Center north of Columbia is in its final phase and most of the manufacturing equipment is installed. The Body Shop, Paint Shop, and Assembly Shop are all being used for the first validation builds.

The Body Shop is the most automated part of the plant. Scout notes more than 750 robots join roughly 160 parts into each body, laying down about 5,000 weld points per vehicle, with AI-supported weld monitoring and a metrology system checking the results. At full capacity, the shop is designed to handle about 40 vehicles per hour.

Bodies then go through an electrified paint shop before landing in final assembly, where they’re married to the chassis and get their wiring, glass, seats, and wheels.

CEO Scott Keogh is clearly happy to have something physical to point to, saying that “what we are building in Blythewood is no longer a promise on paper.”.

Scout also shared photos of a Terra pickup and a Traveler parked inside the plant. Its own fine print notes that they show “concept and validation vehicles” with optional features, so don’t read too much into what’s on display:.

Industry observers note that fair enough. But Scout is also careful about what this stage is. Teams are confirming the equipment is installed and works, and checking engineering, buildability, and parts maturity. Process validation and scaling up to production speed come later. Validation builds will continue “into 2027,” followed by pre-production builds, and then customer deliveries in 2028.

The tech giant says the plant will create more than 4,000 jobs, and it’s spending another $300 million on an onsite supplier park expected to support about 1,000 supplier jobs.

When Keogh laid out the plan in late 2023, Scout said it would start production in 2026 with deliveries shortly after. That was still the target when Scout broke ground in Blythewood in February 2024.

By the Traveler and Terra unveiling in October 2024, production had moved to 2027. Keogh then said in March that he expects the first customer to get a vehicle “sometime in 2028,” and that’s now the official line in Scout’s own press materials.

It might not even be the end of it. Industry forecaster AutoForecast Solutions has the Traveler starting production in September 2028 and the Terra in March 2030. Scout hasn’t confirmed those dates, but it hasn’t given more precise ones either.

Sources indicate that the product itself has also changed under the hood. Scout launched as a pure EV brand, then added the “Harvester” range-extender option at the reveal. According to Keogh, Scout has more than 160,000 reservations, and 87% of them are for the gas-generator version. Those are $100 refundable reservations, not orders.

Der Spiegel reported earlier this year that integrating the range extender, which wasn’t part of the original plan, was among the technical problems pushing the timeline back.

According to recent reports, for comparison, Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in November 2019 and delivered the first ones four years later, a delay that was widely mocked. Scout is now on a similar four-year path from reveal to customer, and that’s for the SUV it’s launching first.

In a recent development, A working body shop with 750 robots isn’t vaporware. Scout has a real factory, a real workforce, and two vehicles that people clearly want. 160,000 reservations is a substantial number for a brand that hasn’t sold a single vehicle in 46 years.

Sources indicate that but validation builds are an early step, not a finish line. Scout still has to go through pre-production, prove its processes, and ramp to rate, and every one of those stages is where latest automakers usually lose time. Rivian and Lucid both learned that the hard way.

According to recent reports, september 28? So we're 23 months away? I'm surprised the validation build yadda yadda stuff is supposed to take so long. It's not like VW doesn't know how to do this stuff, and that's a lot of money and equipment to sit mostly idle while 180,000 reservations holders are waiting for their cars. Maybe they're waiting for the market to change or are considering a whole other brand or product line?

And the market Scout was designed for in 2022 no longer exists. The EV tax credit is gone, and most of Scout’s own reservation holders picked the gas generator. In the US, the range-extender market is still early, unlike in China, where they are already popular.

But by 2028, Ford, Ram, and Jeep all proposal to have range-extended trucks and SUVs on sale. Scout’s main advantage was being early with a cool, rugged, American-built electric truck. That advantage shrinks every quarter.

We’re still rooting for these vehicles. The Traveler and Terra are among the best-looking designs in the segment. But a $100 reservation is easy to walk away from, and the question is how many of those 160,000 people are still waiting in 2028.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, bentley’s first electric car, the Torcal SUV, looks like a hit already. Even though production hasn’t started yet, the $220,000+ EV is sold out for 2027, according to Frank-Steffen Wallier, the firm’s head honcho, quoted by Automotive News.

The British luxury automaker remarked that all available production slots for next year have already been allocated and that the manufacturer is now taking orders that will be delivered in 2028. Bentley didn’t say how many EVs it will build in 2027, but the initial customer response has made the marque quite happy with the outcome.

“Needless to say, we’re very pleased with the response and position we’re in,” a tech giant spokesperson told Automotive News.

That’s great news for Bentley, which isn’t doing great in terms of sales and profit. From January through September, it sold 5,970 cars globally, 17% fewer compared to the same period last year. Meanwhile, the profit dropped by more than half to $54.1 million through the first nine months of the year.

According to recent reports, the Torcal, which is smaller than the Bentayga SUV, is the brand’s cheapest model, though it still costs a pretty penny. The base Torcal starts at $222,495, followed by the more powerful Torcal S at $262,695, and the Torcal First Edition at $300,995. All things considered, Walliser remarked that the smaller size and relatively lower price compared to the Bentayga have attracted newly introduced and younger customers to the brand.

By comparison, the Bentayga starts at $231,150, the Flying Spur sedan starts at $254,850, and the Continental GT two-door starts at $288,750.

According to recent reports, so far, the Torcal S has proved to be the most popular version of the newly introduced EV, but when it comes to personalization, the sky’s the limit. “We see cars spec’d north of 300,000 pounds ($397,086),” said Walliser. “Individual content does not stop in case of an electric car. There have been some assumptions, and some people have been critical if people would be ready to do so.”.

Based on the same underpinnings as the electric Porsche Cayenne, the Bentley Torcal is powered by a 113-kilowatt-hour battery that can be charged at up to 400 kilowatts. It can go from 10% to 80% in less than 20 minutes, and the estimated EPA range is expected to be over 300 miles.

Built on the Premium Platform Electric (PPE) architecture, it has two electric motors that make 810 horsepower and 881 pound-feet of torque in the standard Torcal and a whopping 876 hp and 996 lb-ft of torque in the Torcal S. When the model debuted in September, Bentley said it was the most powerful and quietest model to come out of the factory in Crewe.

To make the Torcal a reality, Bentley invested $463 million to upgrade its factory in England, plus at least the same amount for supply chain preparations and research and development, Walliser said.

Despite the electric SUV’s initial success, the British automaker is still heavily invested in gas and plug-in hybrid models, and the Bentayga isn’t going anywhere. “We have a very good combination with Torcal and Bentayga,” Walliser said. “The segment definitely has space for two cars.”.

According to recent reports, very much when we expected it, Blizzard has officially revealed Diablo 4’s next major expansion at The Game Awards. Lord of Hatred delivers a latest campaign that continues the mainline story, picking up from where Vessel of Hatred left off. Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.

In a recent development, it’s always a massive deal when we get a newly introduced Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been. But perhaps the biggest piece of news out of the Lord of Hatred reveal is that the expansion is bringing not one, but two new classes to the game.

The first of which is The Paladin, whereas the second is being kept under wraps. Even more surprising is that The Paladin is playable right now for anyone who pre-purchases the expansion. This is a well-timed shadow drop, especially given that Diablo 4’s latest season has just kicked off.

In a recent development, the expansion adds a newly introduced region to the world: Skovos, which is where the events of the new campaign will be taking place. This is the first time Skovos has been in a Diablo game. The region is of major significance to the world and lore of the series, as it is the birthplace of the firstborn, home of Lilith and Inaruis.

Sources indicate that lord of Hatred brings a decent number of major systems to Diablo 4. The endgame is getting a big overhaul, headlined by the fresh War Aims feature. Through this, you can effectively design your own endgame grind, creating challenges based on the activities you like and earning rewards along the way.

Endgame activities now also feature their own skill trees, which can be progressed through by creating War Looks for your character featuring each activity. The new endgame activity, Echoing Hatred, is something of horde mode where you must defend against unrelenting waves of enemies.

None of that matters without loot, of course, and the upcoming expansion is bringing back the Horadric Cube, and adding set bonuses using the Talisman system. The long-awaited and highly-requested Loot Filter is also coming to the game with the release of the expansion.

Beyond itemisation, each class’ skill tree will grow with newly introduced bonus skill variants. In fact, the entire skill system is being reworked for all classes - though details are a little sparse at the moment.

You can also expect the level cap to go up, which is very likely necessary to fit all the latest skills and various systems. Blizzard offered a deep dive into the new Paladin class, which you see on the official blog.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Waymo has pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after the California Department of Motor Vehicles ordered the tech giant to pause highway operation in the state, following a viral video showing a Waymo trying to pass a police blockade.

Recent findings suggest that waymo is Google’s robotaxi subsidiary, which has been operating autonomously on public roads in some form since 2017. It has now expanded to 15 areas, recently adding another 250 square miles just last month.

Sources indicate that the vehicles can be hailed through Waymo’s app, and operate with no driver in the driver’s seat, 24/7 in the covered areas. Since it can operate at any time but only within geofenced areas, this counts as “level 4” autonomy, as compared to the level 2 autonomy available on most consumer vehicles.

Until recently, Waymo only operated on city streets. These are more complex than highways, but lower speed. Accidents are more common on city streets than on highways, but can be more spectacular on highways given the higher speeds involved.

Recent findings suggest that most driver assist systems have been rolled out gradually, starting with highways, due to this lower complexity. But Waymo started with city streets first, bucking that trend.

According to recent reports, the tech giant started offering rides on highways late last year, but only in limited markets. It had been testing highway operation for several years prior, typically with a driver and with no public ridership.

Industry observers note that everything was going pretty well, with Waymo declaring its autonomous vehicles have stopped 841 injuries over the course of their 271 million miles of operation. And in terms of competition, Waymo is far ahead of Tesla’s Robotaxi effort.

Sources indicate that but then, the viral internet stepped in. Last week, a video surfaced showing a Waymo trying to pass two police cars who were trying to slow down traffic on I-280 in Northern California. This is one of the main routes through Silicon Valley, and the opening of highway operations drastically reduced ride times in the area.

It has been revealed that the video highlights two police cars behind a construction vehicle, lights on and spread out across the freeway. Then it pans to show a Waymo vehicle moving promptly in the far left lane. One of the officers accelerates and swerves in front of the Waymo vehicle, at which point the Waymo swerves and slows down. (One media citation states that the video seems to have been sped up by the original poster, but we’ve embedded the short local news report on it above).

In response to this, the California DMV contacted Waymo and ordered the organization to pause highway operations while it examines the incident. The order was made on November 11, but wasn’t reported until today.

The DMV cited multiple instances of Waymo vehicles incurring into construction zones, not simply the one viral clip above. It noted that previous incidents had occurred and been noted, and corrective actions were implemented, but that the incidents keep happening.

As a career computer programmer, I struggle to understand the current level of programming testing. Granted, today’s programming is far more complex than in years gone by and the languages are vastly different (I wonder how many coders today can read a memory dump of their programs), but it sure seems like practices like desk checking, and using carefully constructed test data have disappeared. It seems like the mindset is if the compiler produces error free code , the coding must be good. I recall a COBOL programmer where I worked wrote a procedure with 72 nested IF statements. The compiler generated object code with no errors or warnings, but the program would produce invalid output. Turned out the compiler got to a certain point in the procedure and just generated garbage code.

DMV’s pause will remain until Waymo can demonstrate “effective corrective actions” have been taken.

According to recent reports, while the DMV’s order only applies to California highways, Waymo also paused highway operations in other states. It remains operating on city streets in all coverage areas.

Upgrade: Waymo emailed us this statement after it saw this article.

“Safety is at the foundation of everything we do. Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Henry Ford was racing cars before the Mustang, GT40, or even the Ford Motor Company itself existed. Back in 1901, he won his first race behind the wheel of a two-cylinder race car nicknamed “Sweepstakes,” a car that produced just 26 horsepower. 125 years later, Ford has unveiled the 815-horsepower 2028 Mustang GTD 1901—a special edition inspired by the car that helped launch Henry Ford's automotive empire.

The Mustang GTD 1901 has a 789-horsepower advantage over the Sweepstakes car, but the design inspiration is clear. The Mustang GTD 1901 features a distinctive Royal Red exterior and a wide, off-center black racing stripe featuring a bright red centerline. The color combination reverses the original race car's black body and deep red chassis components. Additional diagonal graphics and exposed carbon-fiber elements, including the front splitter, rocker panels, rear diffuser, and wing, complete the exterior look.

According to recent reports, have a seat inside the Mustang GTD 1901, and you immediately realize this is not an ordinary GTD—that is, if there is even such a thing as an ordinary GTD. The first thing you notice are the Mahogany Red leather seats with Race Red stitching. Keep looking, and you’ll see there are also matching red accents on the seatbelts, while the steering wheel receives Mahogany Red faux suede.

Recent findings suggest that the Performance Package is standard equipment on the Mustang GTD 1901. Options include the magnesium wheels, which reduce the unsprung weight by 50.3 pounds. If you want to spice up the interior, you can order the optional titanium trim package, which gets you redesigned titanium shifter paddles that have been lengthened for the 2028 model year. The titanium trim in the GTD, by the way? It comes from retired F-22 fighter jets.

Ford has not revealed how many Mustang GTD 1901’s will be built, or how much they will cost. But we wouldn’t count on seeing too many at your local track day.

A lot has changed since Henry Ford won his first race; horsepower figures, aerodynamics, and suspension technology have come a long way. But the desire of the organization that bears his name to prove itself on the racetrack apparently hasn't changed much at all, and that’s something we’re certainly thankful for.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hyundai revealed the production-ready Neira EV for the first time, a three-row, seven-seat electric SUV set to launch in Indonesia on November 20.

After introducing the Neira Concept at the 2026 Gaikindo Indonesia International Auto Show (GIIAS) in July, Hyundai is gearing up to open pre-orders on November 20.

The Neira is a pretty “massive” deal as Hyundai’s first locally produced seven-seat electric SUV in Indonesia.

Ahead of its official debut on Friday at GAIKINDO Auto Week (GAW) 2026, Hyundai offered a closer look at the upcoming Neira.

The electric SUV is essentially a Hyundai-badged version of the Kia Carens Clavis EV that released last year. Aside from the Hyundai logos, a few minor tweaks to the front and rear ends, and new wheels and headlights, it’s a near replica.

Inside, both are equipped with dual 12.3″ instrument display and center navigation screens, plus an added climate control panel.

Industry observers note that hyundai didn’t reveal battery or powertrain specs, but the Neira is expected to use the same 42 kWh and 51.4 kWh battery packs as the Carens Clavis EV. The former offers an MIDC range of up to 251 mi (404 km), while the latter has up to 304 mi (490 km) on a single charge.

Both batteries can be charged from 10% to 80% in around 39 minutes using a 100 kW DC fast charger.

The Kia Carens Clavis is 4,550 mm long, 1,800 mm wide, and 1,708 mm tall, with a 2,780 mm wheelbase, so Hyundai’s Neira will likely be about the same size, if not slightly bigger.

Hyundai stated the Neira has four key advantages: A higher ground clearance, Hyundai Bluelink connectivity tech, a Blind-spot View Monitor (BVM), and easy third-row access.

A post shared by Hyundai Motors Indonesia (@hyundaimotorindonesia).

Ahead of its upcoming launch, Hyundai is taking the electric 7-seater on a trip to prove its capabilities, going from Kilometer Nol in Banda Aceh to Banda Neira, which is about 4,000 kilometers (about 2,500 miles).

While Hyundai may export the Neira EV to overseas markets like India, don’t expect it to reach the US.

Hyundai already sells a three-row, seven-seat electric SUV, the IONIQ 9, which is built at Hyundai’s Metaplant in Georgia.

The Belgian developer is returning to the series it created with Divinity, a non-numbered sequel that’s designed for new and veteran players alike. The announcement was entirely cinematic, setting the tone for what looks to be the next big thing in the space.

Larian calls Divinity its most ambitious title ever, with the studio striving for a level of depth and breadth we’ve not seen before. This is the next project from the Baldur’s Gate 3 team, after all, so there’s understandably immense anticipation for it.

According to recent reports, divinity is a standalone RPG, and does not require you to have played Divinity: Original Sin, or Divinity: Original Sin 2. If you did, however, you’re going to find the journey extra special because of the continuity it offers.

“We’re ready to bring everything we’ve done previously into one place,” remarked founder and game director, Swen Vincke.

Sources indicate that “This marks the beginning of something with more breadth, depth, and intimacy than anything we’ve created before. We’ve been building toward this moment ever since we took our fate into our own hands. This is the Divinity we’ve always wanted to make and you're going to have loads of fun with it.”.

It has been revealed that beyond that, there’s precious little that’s been revealed for Divinity so far. We don’t know what platforms it’s going to be coming to, nor do we even have a release target. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD’s latest milestone in Japan would barely register on its sales charts back home in China. But selling 10,000 cars in a country dominated by domestic brands is progress, especially when part of that momentum comes from selling a vehicle tailored to what Japanese buyers actually want: a small, practical box on wheels, which also happens to be electric.

The Chinese automaker announced that its cumulative Japanese passenger-car sales had passed 10,000. Its first 5,000 took roughly two and a half years after deliveries began in January 2023. The next 5,000 took about 15 months. That includes its entire lineup, rather than just its newest and arguably most interesting addition: the Racco electric kei car.

It has been revealed that it was bold to challenge Japan’s homegrown manufacturers with something designed specifically for their market and to create the world’s first kei car from a non-Japanese automaker. The Racco’s tall body, tiny footprint, and sliding rear doors follow the familiar Japanese formula for such vehicles. BYD didn’t need to reinvent anything, but its entry needed to be convincing.

According to recent reports, japanese buyers’ initial response to the Racco was encouraging. Released on July 28, it attracted 1,002 orders in two weeks, the fastest order intake of any BYD model in Japan. By the end of August, that had grown to around 1,500. Roughly 80% of buyers chose the range-topping 300 Premium, clearly showing that the cheapest version was less attractive.

Recent findings suggest that BYD credited the Racco with helping deliver record monthly orders across its Japanese lineup in August. Potential buyers who came to see the little EV ended up discovering its other models, too.

Sources indicate that BYD offers six passenger-car models in Japan, and every one has a charging port. Five are fully electric: the Racco kei car, Dolphin hatchback, Seal sedan, Atto 3 crossover, and Sealion 7 SUV. The sixth, the Sealion 6 SUV, is a plug-in hybrid combining a gasoline engine with electric propulsion. That makes the entire lineup electrified, with no gasoline-only cars or conventional, non-plug-in hybrids on offer.

What’s more interesting is comparing the Racco’s sales performance to its main rival, the Nissan Sakura EV, which is also Japan’s best-selling electric car. In October, the Sakura EV sold 878 units, while the Racco sold 607. That’s almost 70% of the volume, marking a 37% rise over September.

Sources indicate that the Nissan Sakura EV was Japan’s electric bestseller for a fourth consecutive year in 2025, but it could lose its crown to the Racco, which gives buyers more battery for less money, at least before subsidies. It starts at ¥2.145 million with a 22.4-kWh pack and 130 miles (210 kilometers) of WLTC range, while the Sakura starts at ¥2.449 million with a 20-kWh battery and 112 miles (180 km).

Even the longer-range Racco, with a 35.8-kWh pack capable of 199 miles (320 km), undercuts the entry-level Nissan at ¥2.398 million. The BYD also gets sliding rear doors instead of the Nissan’s conventional ones. What could help the Sakura stay ahead is the larger government subsidy it benefits from, which can make it cheaper to buy despite its higher sticker price.

It’s a tad early to call the Racco a Japanese sensation, but buyers are clearly interested. This newcomer is already selling roughly seven cars for every ten Sakuras in one month, so it definitely deserves attention.

The trick is matching the present to the person: what they ride, where they go, and what gear they already own.

Give a motorcyclist a gift that makes every ride easier to relive—and can help document the unexpected. It’s a fun way to share adventures and a useful record if a ride takes an unwelcome turn.

This extremely compact starter box is 33% thinner, 27% smaller, and 34% lighter than most portable jump-packs, so it slips right into your pocket. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, arc Raiders is kicking off its last major event of the year. The Cold Snap update arrives moments from now, and it’s perhaps the game’s biggest since its momentous launch in late October. We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including latest content - that all players have access to.

As the name suggests, of course, Cold Snap introduces the upcoming snowfall Map Condition. As part of this, maps will be covered in snow, thanks to snowstorms sweeping across them. For one, snowfall makes it harder to see enemies, but it also turns all lakes solid.

There’s a new mechanic associated with this, and it’s actually similar to Battlefield 6’s Winter Offensive revision. Staying outdoors for too long will cause you to catch frostbite, which slowly drains HP. Embark says you’re going to need to bring more healing items with you on raids, and it doesn’t look like there are firepits that could keep you warm - though staying indoors for a while will help.

Cold Snap arrives alongside limited-time events that will be available until Tuesday, January 13. The snowfall visual upgrade and newly introduced frostbite mechanics are available on Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, Spaceport, and The Blue Gate.

According to recent reports, one of the upcoming events is Flickering Flames, which comes with its own progression track of 25 levels. Content is, of course, unlocked using Merits, which are earned from XP in matches. The other event is the Candleberry Banquet Project, which requires you to donate items found on the surface (including Candleberries).

You’ll earn rewards each time, and each stage completed will reveal a new scene on the banquet table. Likewise, there are cosmetic rewards as part of each stage, and you can use it as a source of Merits, too.

While on the subject, the new enhancement also kicks off a new Raider Deck (battle pass). Available from December 26, The Goalie Raider Deck is pretty much what you’d expect. You’ll find several pages of cosmetic and useful items. The new Deck will be available to all players for free.

Iceland’s first wind farm comes with a water-saving bonus

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1310 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Iceland’s first utility-scale wind farm comes with a useful perk: When the wind picks up, its hydropower reservoirs can save water for later.
  • According to recent reports, vaðölduver Wind Farm plugs straight into the existing Búrfell hydropower infrastructure, sharing 220 kV transmission lines, substations, and access roads.
  • Landsvirkjun, Iceland’s national power company, officially commissioned Vaðölduver on September 15, 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Iceland’s first utility-scale wind farm comes with a useful perk: When the wind picks up, its hydropower reservoirs can save water for later.

According to recent reports, vaðölduver Wind Farm plugs straight into the existing Búrfell hydropower infrastructure, sharing 220 kV transmission lines, substations, and access roads. And Iceland’s windiest months coincide with the time of year when less water flows into its reservoirs.

Landsvirkjun, Iceland’s national power company, officially commissioned Vaðölduver on September 15, 2026. The first 14 turbines are online; another 14 will be installed in a second phase, and the entire wind farm is expected to be operating by the end of 2027.

It has been revealed that once complete, Vaðölduver will have 120 megawatts (MW) of capacity. When I met with the folks at Landsvirkjun in Reykjavik last month, they told me that’s enough to power the equivalent of 90,000 Icelandic households. Vaðalda’s electricity feeds into the grid and is sold through power purchase agreements.

Sources indicate that vaðölduver sits on a lava-and-sand plain east of the Þjórsá River, south of Sultartangi Dam. Landsvirkjun already operates seven hydropower stations in the surrounding Þjórsá and Tungnaá region.

The wind farm was sited in this region of Iceland because the seasons line up nicely.

The winds are strongest in winter, when inflows into hydropower reservoirs can be low. In summer, wind speeds tend to drop, but glacial melt increases water availability for the hydropower system.

When the wind turbines are generating plenty of electricity, Landsvirkjun can ease off hydropower and leave more water in its reservoirs. When the wind drops, hydropower can pick up more of the demand.

That gives the utility more control over when it uses its stored water and helps that water go further.

Sources indicate that german wind turbine maker Enercon manufactured Vaðölduver’s turbines. The project also includes a service and maintenance agreement with Enercon.

Sources indicate that landsvirkjun had a decade of experience operating pilot wind turbines before building Vaðölduver. One big thing they learned: They didn’t need tall towers to find plenty of wind.

According to recent reports, there’s little vegetation or other surface obstructions across this unique, exposed landscape. That allows the turbines to capture productive winds closer to the ground than they could at a more wooded or sheltered location.

“Lower” is relative, of course. The turbines still reach 150 meters (492 feet) at their highest blade tip.

According to recent reports, the wind farm covers 17.1 square kilometers (6.6 square miles). Twenty-five turbines are rated at 4.26 MW each, and the remaining three at 4.5 MW. Landsvirkjun’s presentation puts annual generation at 440 GWh and lists a P50 net efficiency figure of 43%, which is considered strong for onshore wind.

The ability to tap into existing infrastructure was a major factor in Landsvirkjun’s site selection. Where a wind farm goes affects its cost, its environmental footprint, and the people who live nearby.

Recent findings suggest that landsvirkjun also identifies active engagement with communities and other stakeholders as essential to building wind projects. At Vaðölduver, the immediate task is to finish the remaining 14 turbines while the first phase completes its trial runs.

In a recent development, the tech giant sees wind as a potential third pillar of Iceland’s electricity supply alongside hydropower and geothermal. Vaðölduver shows how those resources can work together, with wind adding generation while helping conserve stored water.

Iceland is a world leader in clean energy. It generates nearly 100% of its electricity from renewable sources, combining hydropower fueled by glacial runoff and rivers (around 70%) and geothermal energy (around 30%).

Over 90% of Icelandic households use direct geothermal hot water for space heating and hot water, while the remaining homes use renewable electricity.

But it’s got the same grid capacity challenges as every other country. Adding wind – and anything else that uses power – means paying close attention to what the grid can handle. Iceland has an isolated transmission system, so maintaining stability and ensuring sufficient capacity are increasingly key as the country develops more projects.

While in Reykjavik, I met with the Minister of the Environment, Energy and Climate, Jóhann Páll Jóhannsson, who told me that the Icelandic grid’s capacity is expected to grow from 20 TWh to 24-25 TWh within a decade. Jóhannsson also said that he is pro-data center and that investors are keen to establish more of them in the country.

Recent findings suggest that when I asked Jóhannsson and his team, as well as the teams at Landsvirkjun and publicly owned ON Power, Iceland’s second-largest electricity generator and largest EV charger network, about grid expansion plans to handle that pipeline, they all stated that legislative reforms were being passed to speed up energy permitting processes. There is also financing in place to grow the grid. The physical transmission network is being expanded, but the process is slow because NIMBYism is creating bottlenecks.

In learning about upcoming and completed Icelandic power projects during my visit, it was apparent that the companies in the power and geothermal heat sector regularly collaborate on projects – everyone brings their expertise to the table and works for the common good (yes, really).

But what was striking in discussions about grid expansion was that there seemed to be no intends to pitch in with the Icelandic transmission system operator (TSO), Landsnet hf. It seemed that the plan was to let the TSO come up with the solutions on its own. At most, Jóhannsson’s team said its legislative reform “opened the door” to possible grid innovations.

When I asked the Landsvirkjun team whether they were considering working with the TSO on distributed energy resource (DER) projects like virtual power plants and onsite battery storage for its heavy-industry clients, which make up 80% of its business, they said they hadn’t considered it.

I often wonder why Quebec hasn't followed this strategy. They have huge dams with world-leading power connections, and one of the matter they are facing is a lack of water to refill those dams, due to several years of relative drought. I know it costs a lot to build wind power up north, but siting a project there would re-use their massive investment in power lines. The dams would act as gigantic batteries, because they wouldn't need to drain their reservoirs when the wind is blowing.

It has been revealed that iceland has earned its reputation as a clean energy leader. Bringing that same collaborative and creative approach to expanding its grid would help it keep setting an example for the rest of the world.

Behind the 296 Speciale's cockpit lives a twin-turbocharged V-6 that pairs with a plug-in hybrid system. Together, the gas engine and electric motor combine to produce a whopping 869 horsepower. Power is sent exclusively to the rear wheels through an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. The 296 is capable of driving a short distance on electricity alone, with power drawn from a 5.0-kWh battery pack located under the floor.

Sources indicate that the engine's 8500-rpm redline provides a visceral driving experience, as we learned during a test drive. With the Speciale Aperta, the feeling is even more heightened with the wind ruffling your hair at triple-digit speeds. Four drive modes—eDrive, Hybrid, Performance, and Qualify—provide ascending performance characteristics, and the 296 features communicative electrically assisted power steering and a brake-by-wire system that impart the feel you need for confident high-speed road shredding.

In a recent development, first Row: Inside, the 296 is an exercise in elegant minimalism, except for the steering wheel. Its excessive controls create an ergonomic nightmare. The 296 Speciale gets a special interior that is stripped out for weight-saving purposes. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • The ability to simply plug in at a fast-charging station and start charging within seconds was once a luxury once reserved for Tesla drivers at Superchargers.
  • The patch comes to CCS-equipped General Motors EVs, with NACS-equipped EVs to follow in early 2027.
  • To use Plug & Charge with Electrify America (or any other charging network that has a Plug & Charge agreement with GM), the driver must be registered with GM’s Energy Pass in the MyChevrolet, MyGMC, or MyCadillac app.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The ability to simply plug in at a fast-charging station and start charging within seconds was once a luxury once reserved for Tesla drivers at Superchargers. However, with the advent of Plug & Charge, this seamless operation has come to many other brands, including General Motors. GM revealed Plug & Charge support back in 2022, starting with EVGo. Now, Plug & Charge is all in one space via GM's Energy Pass App, with Ionna and ChargePoint added to the Plug & Charge list in 2026. Today, it confirmed support for the largest CCS fast-charging network in the country: Electrify America.

The patch comes to CCS-equipped General Motors EVs, with NACS-equipped EVs to follow in early 2027.

To use Plug & Charge with Electrify America (or any other charging network that has a Plug & Charge agreement with GM), the driver must be registered with GM’s Energy Pass in the MyChevrolet, MyGMC, or MyCadillac app. The Energy Pass links your EV with a default payment type, allowing charging stations to start the charging event and bill the driver directly without navigating any other app. The driver doesn’t have to do anything but plug in; there’s no need to use a third-party app or fiddle around with a frustrating interface on the charger itself.

It has been revealed that the function works with Ionna, EVGo, and ChargePoint, and now Electrify America. The Energy Pass section of the apps not only controls payment, but serves as a one-stop-shop by showing past charging history and letting you locate and navigate to charging stations.

GM EVs with CCS ports will still have to wait for Plug & Charge support at Tesla Superchargers. But for GM vehicles with NACS ports—including the 2026 Optiq and most 2027 model year cars—can automatically begin charging at Tesla stations.

In order to get more people behind the wheel of EVs, industry leaders have stressed that the ease and quality of charging stops must improve. This goes beyond just making sure there are enough charging stations available and making sure they’re in working order. From start to finish, the charging experience should be easy and painless. Saving time and making things as seamless as possible should help make the charging experience nearly frictionless, which is a good thing for EV adoption.

“Bringing that experience to GM EV drivers is another important step forward. It removes friction from the charging experience and lets customers focus on what matters: plugging in, charging, and getting back on the road.” Robert Barrosa, president and CEO of Electrify America, remarked in a press release.

Recent findings suggest that GM states that on average, the flow of power should start within 45 seconds of plugging in. That is significantly quicker and easier than navigating through a series of menus and apps to start a charging event without Plug & Charge.

Importantly, the addition of Electrify America brings 6,200 chargers that are capable of speeds of up to 350 kW. Some of GM’s largest EVs, like the Chevrolet Silverado EV or Cadillac Escalade IQ, advertise their charging times when connected these ultra-fast charger.

Sources indicate that participation in GM Energy Pass is optional. If the driver doesn’t want to use it, they are free to use the existing charging station apps to charge the vehicle. But it should be easier to use Energy Pass, at least at Electrify America, EVGo, and Ionna stations.

According to recent reports, (Correction 11/18/26 at 10:21 AM ET: This story originally mentioned GM had not rolled out Plug & Charge support for Tesla Superchargers. That is incorrect. GM EVs with native NACS ports already support Plug & Charge at Tesla stations, and CCS vehicles should get the same capability sometime soon.).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that old solar panels have silver and copper worth recovering. A new US recycling company called Jupiter looks to send metals recovered from retired solar panels and data center hardware to Korea Zinc’s refineries, including a $7.4 billion plant planned for Clarksville, Tennessee.

Jupiter joins US solar panel recycler Solarcycle and PedalPoint Recycling, Korea Zinc’s US recycling and metals business, into a single, fully integrated firm. Jupiter says it’s launching with eight certified US facilities, nearly 1 million square feet of processing space, and about 250 employees. It’s also taking on customers from both businesses, including Microsoft, Prologis, and Brookfield.

For a solar farm or data center operator, that means a single company can take equipment out of service, resell parts with remaining useful life, and recycle the rest. Customers can track where the materials go and bring them back into their own supply chains.

It has been revealed that korea Zinc will hold a majority stake. Solarcycle’s Suvi Sharma will lead Jupiter as CEO, and PedalPoint’s Kevin Hahm will be CFO. Microsoft and Prologis Ventures are among Solarcycle’s existing investors.

It has been revealed that as Electrek reported in January, Solarcycle’s Cedartown, Georgia, plant was processing thousands of old solar panels a week when it opened. Solarcycle noted the plant could handle up to 5 gigawatts’ worth of panels annually at full capacity, recovering materials such as glass, aluminum, copper, and silver.

The Tennessee plant adds a US refining step. Korea Zinc is developing the facility, called Project Crucible, with US government backing. It expects to start production in phases in 2029. The plant is designed to process about 1.1 million tons of raw materials per year and produce roughly 540,000 tons of finished products.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere.
  • Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.
  • According to recent reports, to start with, today’s enhancement finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a upcoming conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

According to recent reports, to start with, today’s enhancement finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer mentioned the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock newly introduced Raider Decks immediately after release.

The good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

It has been revealed that speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

According to recent reports, the Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark says this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

Industry observers note that as for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

And, of course, it wouldn’t be a significant Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

Industry observers note that the Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this revision, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.

#40528. Potatoes grown in moon dirt are as nutritious as Earth potatoes

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (561 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci ↗ Open Full Page

Potatoes grown in moon dirt are as nutritious as Earth potatoes

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (561 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Astronauts living in the first permanent lunar base may see a sizable number of spuds on their dinner plates.
  • “We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter,” Aymeric Goyer, an OSU botanist and study co-author, said in a statement.
  • Recent findings suggest that even in a controlled habitat, life on the moon will be physically demanding for astronauts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Astronauts living in the first permanent lunar base may see a sizable number of spuds on their dinner plates. In a study published today in the journal npj Microgravity, botanists at Oregon State University (OSU) proved it’s possible to grow healthy, edible potatoes in simulated moon soil with the help of everyday worms. Importantly, the team also identified the proper proportions of lunar regolith and compost needed to produce potato yields similar to those grown on Earth.

“We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter,” Aymeric Goyer, an OSU botanist and study co-author, said in a statement. “That’s an important step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the Moon.”.

Recent findings suggest that even in a controlled habitat, life on the moon will be physically demanding for astronauts. They’ll require carefully maintained, nutritious diets to keep them healthy, but it’s not as simple as sending them off packed with calorically dense prepackaged meals. Cargo room on spacecraft is limited and costly, and the desolate lunar surface isn’t exactly hospitable to agriculture. In addition to constant bombardment by cosmic and solar radiation, temperatures can swing anywhere between 250 degrees and -410 degrees Fahrenheit.

Indoor horticulture will also be challenging. Lunar regolith is an annoyingly powdery substance composed of sharp-edged, miniscule particles created over billions of years of asteroid impacts, but little else. With essentially no organic material at all, the dust alone isn’t capable of supporting plant life.

While it is easy enough to combine that lunar regolith with agricultural additives, researchers weren’t sure if these could overcome moon soil’s heavy metals and irradiation. To test it, Goyer and his colleagues first obtained simulated lunar regolith made to resemble the samples collected during the Apollo missions. Regolith composition varies by region on the moon, so they selected five different types based on darker lunar mare dust and the lighter lunar highland soil. They then mixed the mock moon dust with vermicompost, the nutrient-rich soil created when worms break down organic materials. Next, they planted potatoes in various ratios of regolith and vermicompost, and monitored their growth. As a control, the team even planted potatoes in soil taken from Hermiston, Oregon, an area famous for some of the world’s highest spud yields.

The team found that composite soil with only 30 percent vermicompost was enough to produce potato crops comparable to those farmed on Earth. Their findings suggest the supplemental organics bind to the regolith’s heavy metals, which shield the plants and minimize any damage to their roots.

“We believe the compost helps balance some of the toxicity we see in lunar regolith,” added OSU botanist and study co-author David Handy.

But bushels of moon potatoes only go so far if they lack any real nutritional value. Even here, the lunar simulations offered promising results, particularly when it came to glycoalkaloids. The naturally forming potato toxins can cause green skin discoloration, but analysis indicated no statistically relevant rise in glycoalkaloids for the lunar crops.

With the potato viability debate settled, Goyer’s team will next compare 10 specific spud varieties grown in simulated lunar regolith to determine the most nutritious and resilient options for NASA astronomers.

REO Runabout vs. Slate Truck: Which Sub-$30,000 Truck Is Better?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (810 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that like the idea of a Slate but don't want an EV?
  • According to recent reports, first, let's look at price.
  • The cheapest REO you can get will be the Runabout T4X, which costs $21,500*.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that like the idea of a Slate but don't want an EV? Well, an upstart from Dallas, Texas has just the thing for you. That is, if it ever becomes a reality. Startup organization REO recently unveiled renderings of its new truck, dubbed the Runabout. It's a similar idea to Slate, with just one basic frame, three different body variants to choose from, no frills, a bunch of customization, and a sub-$30,000 price tag. The main difference is that that Runabout uses a four-cylinder gas engine, rather than electric motors. So how does it compare to Slate?

According to recent reports, first, let's look at price. The most basic Slate you can get—cheekily called "The Blank Slate"—costs $24,950, and it's a two-door pickup with nothing more than some seats, a steering wheel, a battery, and a single rear electric motor to get you around. There's no radio, power windows, or screens to speak of.

The cheapest REO you can get will be the Runabout T4X, which costs $21,500*. Note the asterisk, as REO claims the current listed price is an estimate, and the company has no factory or clear prepares for getting it to market. For that shockingly low price, it's estimated that you'll get a four-cylinder engine, a choice of either a six-speed manual or automatic transmission, and mechanical four-wheel drive. It's a two-door, two-seat pickup with drop-down sides for the bed, like a Kei truck.

What four-cylinder engine will the Runabout have and which manufacturer will supply it? REO isn't saying. There are far more questions than answers so far. REO does say that it has a "targeted powertrain life of 500,000 miles." To quote myself reading that in the press release: "lol.".

According to recent reports, while Slate uses a hybrid body-on-frame style chassis, the REO has an old-school ladder frame, like a classic pickup. It's similar to slate in that it offers modular body styles, but with key differences. There's a two-door pickup and an SUV version, like Slate, but there's also a four-door pickup, which Slate doesn't have. REO claims its truck has solid rear axles, too, to give it more off-road credibility.

The design isn't bad, even if it looks like a Grand Theft Auto version of an Australian-market Land Cruiser, but that's to be expected. REO hired longtime automotive designer Frank Stephenson, whose previous work includes the first BMW-owned Mini Cooper, the Maserati MC12, and the McLaren P1. Overall, it looks handsome enough and utilitarian, even if all the photos are just renders at this point.

It has been revealed that inside, REO's truck is said to be pretty barebones (it hasn't been revealed yet), but not as barebones as Slate's. There's a digital screen for gauges and one for navigation, but everything else has a physical control. You're probably wondering if it has power or hand-crank windows. REO used its press release to throw a little shade: " Each model will feature power windows for convenience: hand-cranks are best left to others.".

The entire idea behind REO is to offer the sort of basic pickups customers loved in the '80s and '90s, trucks that were simple utilitarian workhorses and nothing else. It's an admirable goal, especially given how expensive pickups have become. But do customers want to go backward in powertrain technology, especially with affordable mainstream electric trucks like the Ford Fathom coming to market soon?

So for less money, you can get a potentially more capable truck, in a similar configuration as the Slate, with a bit of extra interior comfort. But you lose the electric powertrain, which reduces maintenance and fuel costs. Instead, you'll have to make due with a generic four-cylinder of some sort. There is one big "if," though. You can only buy one if REO ever actually makes it. Sure, having a design by Frank Stephenson helps it feel more real, but just because they found the money to pay him to design something doesn't mean they'll actually get around to building it.

Industry observers note that slate is already here, it's ready to launch production vehicles soon. We've seen them in person, touched them, and tested them. Until REO can actually muster a viable product, it should probably avoid throwing anymore shade in its press releases.

Electric power tool brand Greenworks is expanding its battery-forward lineup in a huge way with the launch of OPTIMUS, an all-new, go-anywhere electric side-by-side utility vehicle that packs over 100 equivalent hp and a 40 mph top speed.

First shown at Equip Exposition 2026 in Kentucky last month, the newly redesigned Greenworks OPTIMUS UTV is the biggest, baddest, and newest addition to the tech giant’s battery-backed commercial ecosystem. Greenworks claims the newly introduced SxS brings together the brand’s purpose-built equipment and power platforms and is designed to work across the demands of its professional property maintenance customers.

“OPTIMUS has always been about pushing battery power beyond what the industry expects, and the UTV is a natural extension of that vision,” claims Yin Chen, CEO of Greenworks. “We’re bringing professionals more ways to put battery power to work, from the equipment they use to maintain properties to the utility vehicles and charging systems that support their entire operation.”.

Greenworks’ OPTIMUS is built around the company’s 400V high-voltage electrical platform and mates a pair of compact electric motors that combine for 110 equivalent (?) hp. Those motors draw power from a 19 kWh lithium-ion battery pack with enough efficiency to hit a 40 MPH top speed and cover up to 68 miles of range under typical operating conditions.

When it’s time to haul, OPTIMUS offers buyers a 2,500 lb. towing capacity and 1,300 lb. payload capacity along with 11 full inches of ground clearance and a beefy, 6,000 lb. electric winch. Independent suspension, oversized all-terrain tires, torque vectoring differentials, and multiple terrain modes round out the spec sheet and a picture of a machine that’s designed to handle some seriously demanding off-road applications.

Looks expensive but for a gov or tech giant leasing or buying a upcoming utv probably price completive with less headache.
