💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that decades before the advent of the soft-roader, Subaru was building everyday cars with a limited amount of extra off-road capability.
  • Naturally, Subaru has now combined the two by offering a Forester Hybrid in Wilderness trim.
  • Industry observers note that our expert editors test every vehicle we review.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that decades before the advent of the soft-roader, Subaru was building everyday cars with a limited amount of extra off-road capability. So it should be no surprise that its Wilderness line of slightly more capable crossovers has been a hit. So, too, has Subaru’s integration of hybrid systems, in an era when buyers of volume cars such as the Forester are happy to get their hands on anything that means greater efficiency.

Naturally, Subaru has now combined the two by offering a Forester Hybrid in Wilderness trim. The recipe seems like a sales hit waiting to happen, but is it worth the extra complexity?

Industry observers note that our expert editors test every vehicle we review. Read more about how we test and review cars here.

Recent findings suggest that subaru finally brought a hybrid powertrain to the Forester for the 2025 model year. A new Wilderness was introduced a few months later, but it lacked the gas-electric system available on the basic car. The Forester Wilderness Hybrid combines the two, allowing Subaru to offer a system peak of 194 horsepower from a 2.5-liter flat-four and a 1-kWh battery pack.

EPA-estimated fuel economy is down slightly from the basic Forester Hybrid, but the 33 mpg city and 29 mpg highway are still both solid numbers for a crossover with 9.3 inches of ground clearance and Yokohama Geolander all-terrain tires. For most buyers, that improvement alone should justify the price, which is $1000 more than the basic Forester Wilderness.

Powertrain: 2.5-liter Atkinson-cycle flat-four, lithium-ion hydride battery pack.

Power: 194 hp @ 5600 rpm (peak system output).

Transmission: continuously variable automatic, all-wheel drive.

EPA mpg: 33 city, 29 highway, 31 combined.

Sources indicate that befitting the Wilderness Hybrid’s soft-roader credentials, the media drive took place on the dirt, grass, and gravel roads of a private ranch. While this made for beautiful scenery, it did little to showcase what the car could do as a daily driver or challenge its off-road capabilities.

Those capabilities did impress on a more technical off-roading course that Subaru built for the event, although that comes with the caveat that the organization presumably built the course with the car’s limits in mind. Even though this is ultimately still a relatively conventional crossover with nothing like the articulation of a more extreme off-roader, the all-terrain tires were capable of handling substantial ruts and steep hill descents.

Approach, break-over, and departure angles of 23.5, 20.6, and 25.5 degrees, respectively, are identical to the nonhybrid Forester Wilderness. This hybrid crossover has the clearance to get over obstacles a car camper or kayaker might find on the trail to their favorite outdoor-recreation spot. The biggest frustration here was the low resolution of the X-Drive off-road menus built into the infotainment screens, a feature that felt behind the respectable capabilities of the crossover itself.

Sources indicate that while the off-road performance is what sets the Wilderness apart from its more pedestrian Forester Hybrid brethren, limited on-road testing suggests that the car feels similar in everyday situations. Given the all-terrain tires, that’s a solid achievement, even if the end result is still relative mediocrity. This Forester is no performance car, and anyone who might have been expecting a canyon carver will instead have to make do with relaxed acceleration and a frustrating continuously variable automatic transmission.

It has been revealed that the Forester is a tentpole for Subaru because it combines the basic compact-crossover shape today’s buyers want with some degree of utility in all forms. The Wilderness goes one step further in providing even more capability, but its day-to-day strength will be how little it sacrifices to do that.

Industry observers note that the Forester Wilderness Hybrid drops 5 mpg of efficiency in the city in comparison to the standard Forester Hybrid, for 33 mpg. The basic Forester Wilderness, by contrast, gets just 24 mpg in the city. The hybrid remains relatively comfortable and quiet on the road too, which is great news for buyers who do not want to hear harsh noises from all-terrain tires and the unique drone of a Subaru boxer engine all day.

Industry observers note that still, the Wilderness line is differentiated by its capabilities. Buyers looking for a soft-roader do expect to use the car on a trail every so often, which makes the Wilderness Hybrid’s lack of a spare tire a major glitch. Since components of the hybrid system are packed where a spare would go on a normal Wilderness, buyers of this car will either have to find another way to carry a fifth tire or contend with the reality that a flat could derail their outdoor adventures in a worse way than the same problem would in the nonhybrid model.

That missing spare tire is one of two major drawbacks for the Wilderness Hybrid. The other is the towing capacity, down from 3500 pounds to just 1500. Both of these are serious limitations for buyers who have certain use cases in mind for their soft-roader, but neither is necessarily a problem for the average buyer. The price difference is not negligible, but fuel savings should cover the difference in cost within a few years. For most buyers, that makes the Hybrid the obvious choice.

Recent findings suggest that buyers looking at other hybrid soft-roaders could also consider the latest Toyota RAV4 Woodland and the Honda CR-V Trailsport. The Subaru is the only one of the three hybrids with conventional full-time all-wheel drive, although that specific differentiator is not necessarily a game changer for buyers who will be spending most of their time on the street. For those who do need to venture a little further a little more often, though, the Forester Hybrid Wilderness seems like the strongest choice.

Subaru’s Wilderness models are sold with synthetic StarTex interiors meant to be easily cleaned, and this particular vehicle even includes a synthetic steering-wheel cover in lieu of the usual leather. This is a small detail for most, but it does mean that the cabin is entirely vegan. For some very specific buyers, however, that one detail could make all the difference.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the Kia Besta EV hit the roads in 1986 as the brand’s first fully electric vehicle.
  • Kia wanted to design a fresh vehicle for the 1986 Asian Games, which were held in Seoul, South Korea, one that did not emit any toxic fumes in front of runners.
  • Recent findings suggest that so, it created the Besta EV.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Kia Besta EV hit the roads in 1986 as the brand’s first fully electric vehicle. 40 years later, Kia continues to “lead the pack” with a full lineup of EVs ranging from entry-level cars and SUVs to three-row models, and just about everything in between.

Kia wanted to design a fresh vehicle for the 1986 Asian Games, which were held in Seoul, South Korea, one that did not emit any toxic fumes in front of runners.

Recent findings suggest that so, it created the Besta EV. The Besta van was initially developed 40 years ago by Kia’s Central Research Institute as the successor to the popular Bongo van, which is still sold in Korea and other markets today.

Unlike the Bongo, it was developed using Kia’s in-house tech rather than sourced from another automaker and rebadged as its own.

Kia swapped the 2.0L four-cylinder diesel engine for a 35 kWh battery and electric motor, which provided a range of more than 26 miles (42 km) on a single charge.

While the Besta EV was never actually sold to the public, it laid the groundwork and offered an early glimpse at Kia’s shift to electrification.

Recent findings suggest that the first mass-produced Korean EV certified for commercial sale was the Kia Pride EV in 1993. In 2011, the Ray EV became Kia’s first series-production electric car.

Kia expanded its electrification ambitions to Europe and the UK in 2014 with the first-generation Soul EV, the beloved boxy, funky crossover that was discontinued after the 2025 model year.

The Korean automaker has come a long way since the Besta EV, with a full lineup of electric vehicles ranging from compact cars to mid-size and three-row SUVs, vans, and just about everything in between.

Kia now offers an electric option for nearly everyone with seven-passenger EVs on sale in the UK and Europe, including the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, and PV5 Passenger van.

It has been revealed that with its first software-defined vehicle (SDV) and a new B-segment electric hatchback set to launch by the end of 2027, Kia has no plans to slow down. On top of this, Kia will expand its PBV lineup with the PV7 next year, a larger sibling to the PV5.

Four decades after the Besta EV arrived, Kia mentioned it continues to “lead the pack today” with one of the most diverse all-electric EV lineups of any brand.

Through October, Kia has sold over 135,000 EVs in the UK, with fully electric vehicles now accounting for over 37% of total sales.

Thanks to its new EV lineup, Kia became “Europe’s fastest-growing top 10 passenger-car brand.” According to the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association, Kia registered 377,078 vehicles between January and August 2026, up 9% compared to the same period last year.

Sjoerd Knipping, Chief Operating Officer of Kia Europe, said the growth is thanks to having “one of the broadest and most advanced electrified line-ups in Europe.”.

In the US, Kia released the compact EV3 (check out our review of it) this year, starting at just $29,890. It joins the EV6, EV9, and Niro EV in Kia’s US electric vehicle lineup.

Ford Just Started Fathom LFP Battery Production In Michigan. It's A Big Deal

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (776 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ford just reached a critical milestone in the development of its Fathom electric truck.
  • In a recent development, one can’t overstate how vital the Marshall plant is for Ford.
  • It has been revealed that it has an annual production capacity of 20 gigawatt-hours and can manufacture 50 battery packs every hour.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ford just reached a critical milestone in the development of its Fathom electric truck. The tech giant has started manufacturing low-cost lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) battery packs at its $3 billion BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, located a couple hours west of Detroit, in Marshall, MI. These are production-grade LFP batteries which will first be used in Fathom prototypes before full-scale manufacturing begins next year.

In a recent development, one can’t overstate how vital the Marshall plant is for Ford. It’s the first plant in the U.S. to manufacture LFP batteries for mainstream consumer vehicle use domestically. LG Energy Solution also produces LFP batteries in the U.S.—supplying to GM and Tesla—but they’re dedicated to stationary energy storage systems. Ford’s 2 million-square-foot facility is dedicated to automotive LFP batteries.

It has been revealed that it has an annual production capacity of 20 gigawatt-hours and can manufacture 50 battery packs every hour. It’s a vertically integrated plant, where materials like raw lithium and iron-phosphate powder go in one end, and fully assembled, ready-to-install battery packs come out the other. All anode and cathode production, as well as major production processes in between, happen inside the plant.

Alan Clarke, the vice president of advanced development projects at Ford, said the manufacturer is moving fast to bring the Fathom to the market. In a relatively short time period, he claimed, Ford had developed the all-new Universal EV Platform that will underpin its future EVs, an all-new production system at the Louisville Assembly Plant, and domestic LFP battery production.

“Not having a team that existed to have a battery factory, a unicasting factory, an entirely newly introduced most automated vehicle production facility that Ford's ever produced in less than five years would be I think faster than China speed,” Clarke said during a media roundtable at the BlueOval Battery Park Michigan on Tuesday.

Clarke previously worked at Tesla for 12 years, helping create the Model S, followed by development work for the Model X, Model Y, Model 3, and Cybertruck.

BlueOval Battery Park Michigan drone photo.

I toured Ford’s LFP plant this week, and I think it’s one of the most advanced, highly-automated battery facilities in the U.S. Michigan, America’s automotive manufacturing hub for a century, certainly hasn’t seen anything like it in its history.

Part of the reason why the facility is so cutting-edge comes from Ford’s LFP licensing deal with China’s CATL, the world’s largest and the most advanced battery maker. The U.S. has been lagging behind China and Europe in the battery technology race. Ford is now bringing that technical know-how back to the U.S. even if that means licensing technology from CATL.

More importantly, Ford officials said the new plant is fully compliant with the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) rules. Raw materials used to make batteries here do not come from what the U.S. government designates as Foreign Entities of Concern (FEOC). Even though the technology is from CATL, the critical materials aren’t sourced from U.S. FEOCs such as China, Russia and North Korea. (China controls the vast majority of the global critical materials supply chain.).

Final inspection of the Ford Fathom's LFP prismatic cells.

Industry observers note that the plant is fully owned and operated by Ford, but CATL engineers helped the firm set up thousands of incredibly complex production tools. They’re also helping train workers to operate high-tech equipment and install tight quality control systems to help Ford deliver the affordable EV that it has long promised. The prismatic LFP cell itself is unique to Ford and not something that exists in CATL’s global portfolio.

Meng Wang, the director and chief engineer of battery cell industrialization at Ford summed up the CATL partnership well. “To shorten our time to market, we decided to learn from the best,” Wang noted. “Throughout the process, CATL passed on critical knowledge to Ford, including the equipment functions, manufacturing process, and also quality controls.”.

Preorders for the Ford Fathom will begin early 2027 and production and deliveries are expected to begin by the end of next year.

Sources indicate that we at Car and Driver pride ourselves on our institutional knowledge and in-depth testing. It's why we've spent the last 70 years analyzing, reviewing, and testing the latest vehicles on the market.

Industry observers note that if you want to know the ins and outs of just about any car sold in the United States, then you come to Car and Driver. And now, if you want to buy a fresh or used vehicle, then you . . . come to Car and Driver.

In a recent development, specifically, the Car and Driver Marketplace. Powered by Autotrader, which offers one of the largest inventories of vehicle listings on the web, C/D Marketplace makes us a one-stop shop for researching and purchasing a vehicle.

In a recent development, not sure where to find or how to use our Marketplace? Then we've got you covered. Read on to see how easy it is to find your next car using C/D Marketplace.

It has been revealed that car and Driver Marketplace is for all shoppers in the market for a new or used vehicle—enthusiast and non-enthusiast alike. Whether you’re looking for a sports car to scratch your driving itch, a minivan or SUV for hauling the family around, or a pickup truck to take to work, you can use Car and Driver Marketplace to search through thousands of new- and used-vehicle listings.

Car and Driver Marketplace is a vehicle shopping tool for consumers in the market for a new or used vehicle. We have thousands of new- and used-vehicle listings for vehicles being sold across the nation.

Whether you’re daydreaming about a certain make or model of vehicle, in the early stages of researching your next vehicle, or ready to reach out to sellers to purchase a latest vehicle, you’ll find there’s no wrong time to use Car and Driver Marketplace.

Industry observers note that powered by Autotrader, Car and Driver Marketplace hosts one of the web’s largest inventories of new- and used-vehicle listings. But Car and Driver Marketplace doesn’t just help you find a new or used vehicle; it also helps you purchase one. With the ability to message sellers directly, submit offers, and calculate lease and finance payments, Car and Driver Marketplace can support just about the entirety of your car-buying journey from start to finish.

Enter the C/D Marketplace in one of two ways: from our home page or by going to caranddriver.com/cars-for-sale (feel free to bookmark it too).If you opt to enter C/D Marketplace from our home page, click on "Shop for Cars" on the top left of the page. Using a mobile device? Tap the drop-down menu on the top left of the page, then press "Shop for Cars" at the top of the list.

Sources indicate that once on the C/D Marketplace page, we recommend adjusting the filters. They appear on the left side of the page on desktop, and as a dropdown menu on the top left of the page on mobile.

Don't let the sheer number of filter options intimidate you. You can mess with as many or as few of them as you like. We do recommend at least filling out the "Location" field with your ZIP code and adjusting the radius of your search, which you can set from as few as 50 miles to the entire United States.

Some filters might be more crucial to you than others, such as the one labeled "Price & Payments" that allows you to set a price range for your search.

In a recent development, that's easy to figure out if you're a cash buyer, but what if you're looking to finance or lease your next car? Then click on the "Set Budget" link (or "Update Budget" if you want to make adjustments to your already set budget). Toggle "Show Payments on Listings" too.

After you click the "Set Budget" (or "Upgrade Budget") link, a pop-up window appears. It allows you to input your budget, the trade-in value of your vehicle (assuming you have a trade), and the amount you're planning to spend toward the down payment.

It has been revealed that once you enter this information, you have the option to further granulate your monthly payment looks for the car you're interested in. You can set your budget for either leasing or financing. (Click the "Return to Dashboard" link after making an individual adjustment to get back to the pop-up window's home page.).

Industry observers note that now, go to the upper right side of the screen and click on the "Sort By" drop-down menu to make sure C/D Marketplace is presenting listings in your preferred order. Mobile users will find this setting under the "Filters" menu at the top left of the screen.

The page defaults to sorting by relevance to your query, but you can also have it sort by price (lowest or highest), distance (closest), date (oldest or newest posted), vehicle mileage (lowest or highest), or model year (newest or oldest).

You're ready to scroll through listings now. See something you like? Click on it! Here's an example of what an individual listing page looks like. We picked a listing of our EV of the Year–winning 2025 Porsche Taycan in GTS form as an example.

As seen here, individual listings allow you to open up additional images of the vehicle, see basic specs (more detailed ones are available if you scroll farther down the page), adjust your spend, and even send a message or an offer to the seller.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that kia has cemented itself as one of the world’s premier electric vehicle manufacturers.
  • Kia’s first EV introduced in 1986 and was very crucial for several reasons.
  • Ahead of the 1986 Asian Games, Kia decided to develop a marathon broadcast vehicle that could keep pace with runners and house timekeeping and camera equipment—all while not disturbing runners with exhaust fumes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that kia has cemented itself as one of the world’s premier electric vehicle manufacturers. And it's spent longer experimenting with EVs than you probably think. This week, Kia marked 40 years since its first EV hit the road. It highlights just how far the automaker—and the EV industry—has come.

Kia’s first EV introduced in 1986 and was very crucial for several reasons. It was based on a van called the Besta. This was Kia’s first van developed in-house, replacing the Mazda-based Bongo van that it was making before.

Ahead of the 1986 Asian Games, Kia decided to develop a marathon broadcast vehicle that could keep pace with runners and house timekeeping and camera equipment—all while not disturbing runners with exhaust fumes. So the automaker ripped out the Besta's 2.0-liter diesel engine and replaced it with an electric motor and 35 kilowatt-hours worth of lead-acid batteries.

It has been revealed that the range wasn’t great, but it was enough to cover the whole 26.2-mile marathon on one charge. Hyundai indicates it had around 75 miles of range and a top speed of 56 mph. It made another appearance at the 1998 Seoul Olympics.

Recent findings suggest that most importantly, Kia claims the Besta EV was South Korea’s first-ever EV. The brand would go on to continue developing EV prototypes like the 1991 Sonata EV and 1992 Excel. In 1993, the Pride EV hatchback became Korea’s first EV certified for commercial sale, although it didn't get a full production run. This car, which you may have known in gas form as the Ford Festiva, had an (estimated) 17.4 kWh battery and solar panels that Kia said were good for almost ten miles of additional range.

The Kia Ray was the brand's first production electric vehicle, launching in 2011 with 86 miles of range.

Recent findings suggest that eventually, Kia made its first true production model, the Ray EV, in 2011. It had a 16.4 kWh battery pack and 86 miles of range. Three years later in 2014, the Soul EV came to market, bringing a Kia EV to the U.S. for the first time. And things really took off from there.

There’s only a four-year gap between the 93-mile Soul EV and the 238-mile Niro EV. In a relatively short amount of time, Kia’s EVs went from being useful as a second car to having enough range to be a sole vehicle. Today the company has a deep and competitive line of EV models, including the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6 and EV9—although we are missing some of those options in the U.S.

And forty years after the Besta, Kia is back to making electric vans. The PV5 went on sale last year, offering several battery options and a range of up to 258 miles WLTP. Sales are off to a promising start; Kia says it sold some 57,000 of them in the van's first 14 months on the market.

  • For starters, Ford’s standard 5.0-liter V-8 is mated here to a 3.0-liter Whipple supercharger for a total output of 840 horsepower and 615 lb-ft of torque.
  • It has been revealed that “The Vintage Fastback is a car we’ve always wanted to build.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that taking a vintage muscle car and swapping in modern components to make it run better or add power is a story as old as, well, the LS2 V-8. Vintage Modern’s newly introduced Fastback Mustang turns that formula upside down—by swapping old-school body parts onto a modern S650-generation Mustang GT. But the Vintage Modern Fastback, officially revealed on Wednesday at Retromobile New York, is more than just a body kit.

For starters, Ford’s standard 5.0-liter V-8 is mated here to a 3.0-liter Whipple supercharger for a total output of 840 horsepower and 615 lb-ft of torque. Prospective buyers can choose between a six-speed manual transmission with rev matching or a 10-speed automatic with steering-wheel-mounted paddle shifters. Other high-end Mustang features like active-valve performance exhaust with four sound modes, MagneRide adaptive suspension, six selectable drive modes, and Brembo performance brakes are also standard fare.

It has been revealed that “The Vintage Fastback is a car we’ve always wanted to build. We’ve blended classic-inspired design with modern safety, technology, and performance,” remarked Chau Nguyen, founder and CEO of Vintage Modern. “This is what Vintage Modern was created to do.”.

Recent findings suggest that even though the bones of the Fastback are from a current-generation Mustang, the heavily modified vehicle still underwent crash testing to meet applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. This retro-inspired Mustang features eight airbags, crumple zones, side-impact beams, electronic stability control, traction control, and anti-lock brakes. That’s more than most restomod Mustang owners can say.

Sources indicate that most of the custom body panels, including the functional hood scoop, are carbon fiber; the only obviously metal pieces are the billet-aluminum grille, door handles, mirrors, and twin auxiliary driving lights. Similarly, the interior of the retro Fastback build features Alcantara and billet-aluminum trim over three different seat upholsteries: pleated, diamond-quilted, or woven. Each buyer can choose from more than 40 standard paint colors, as well as paint-to-sample finishes and stripe options, along with their own interior configurations; Vintage Modern is also offering an optional JL Audio premium sound system and leather-trimmed floor mats.

Vintage Modern’s carbon-fiber body panels are hand-made in Detroit before being assembled and finished at its Atlanta facility; all told, each unit requires around 900 hours of hands-on labor. The builder has massive looks, too; it indicates it has plans to move into a upcoming factory three times the size of its existing facility, hire more than 100 additional team members, and triple production capacity within two years.

No pricing details about the Vintage Modern Fastback were available at the time of publication, but we’ll update this story when we learn more.

Recent findings suggest that A Upcoming York transplant hailing from the Pacific Northwest, Emmet White has a passion for anything that goes: cars, bicycles, planes, and motorcycles. After learning to ride at 17, Emmet worked in the motorcycle industry before joining Autoweek in 2022 and Road & Track in 2024. The woes of alternate side parking have kept his fleet moderate, with a 2014 Volkswagen Jetta GLI and a BMW 318i E30 street parked in his Queens community.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, most studios wouldn't pick the week between The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and GTA 6 to launch their debut game, but Denkiworks did.
  • It has been revealed that the Kyoto studio's debut follows Pon, a tanuki delivering packages by BMX while restoring a shrine before a summer festival.
  • In an interview with GamesIndustry.biz, Denkiworks co-founder and game director Liam Edwards explained why the team stuck with November and what it hopes happens once players have had their fill of the bigger games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, most studios wouldn't pick the week between The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and GTA 6 to launch their debut game, but Denkiworks did. Its cozy adventure, Tanuki: Pon's Summer, arrived on November 10, and the three-person studio states there were good reasons to take the risk.

It has been revealed that the Kyoto studio's debut follows Pon, a tanuki delivering packages by BMX while restoring a shrine before a summer festival. It's a very different game from Rockstar's crime epic, but that doesn't make finding an audience in November any easier.

In an interview with GamesIndustry.biz, Denkiworks co-founder and game director Liam Edwards explained why the team stuck with November and what it hopes happens once players have had their fill of the bigger games.

The date wasn't chosen to challenge Nintendo or Rockstar. Denkiworks first aimed for summer but needed longer to finish the game and prepare a multiplatform release. October became the next target, until platform marketing opportunities made November more attractive, Edwards explained.

It has been revealed that less competition doesn't always mean better visibility for a small studio. Denkiworks also secured a publishing deal with Critical Reflex and an early agreement to bring Tanuki: Pon's Summer to Xbox Game Pass. Both offered ways to reach players beyond what the studio could manage alone.

According to recent reports, there was another practical hurdle. Denkiworks wanted the game available across PC and consoles at launch, which is a lot to ask of a three-person core team. With help from its publisher, an external porting team handled the Xbox, original Switch, and PlayStation versions, while Denkiworks concentrated on PC and Switch 2. Launching everywhere took coordination, but it also meant players wouldn't have to wait for their preferred platform.

Recent findings suggest that then came the surprise. Nintendo released its Ocarina of Time remake on November 5, just five days before Tanuki: Pon's Summer. Edwards says the studio couldn't have anticipated the move. That left Tanuki squeezed between Nintendo's game and GTA 6, which launches November 19.

Industry observers note that that may be the more awkward overlap. Edwards believes the audience for Pon's laid-back Japanese adventure is more likely to intersect with Zelda players than with people counting down the days to GTA 6. And Ocarina of Time's enormous opening indicates just how much attention Nintendo's game has commanded. Trying to compete for the same players in the same week isn't an enviable position for a studio of this size.

Still, it's worth separating the unexpected Zelda release from the studio's own decision. Denkiworks chose November for the opportunities it offered. It didn't knowingly set out to challenge both giants, and Edwards isn't pretending the team can match their marketing budgets.

Rather than trying to win launch week, Edwards hopes Tanuki: Pon's Summer can stick around in people's minds. He described the game as a "lovely little underdog" and suggested that word of mouth could help it find an audience after players have moved on from Zelda and GTA 6. That's a different kind of release strategy from trying to dominate the charts on day one.

It has been revealed that denkiworks is betting that Pon's charm will do some of the work. Alongside delivering mail and performing BMX tricks, players can get to know the island's residents, take part in activities, and rebuild the Great Tanuki Shrine. With so many major releases competing for attention, Pon's laid-back adventure offers something quite different.

According to recent reports, for Denkiworks, the goal isn't to beat Zelda or GTA 6. It's to make a game people remember when they're ready to play something else.

For Denkiworks, the goal isn't to beat Zelda or GTA 6. It's to make a game people remember when they're ready to play something else.

Sources indicate that that approach isn't risk-free. Launching next to two huge games could bury Tanuki before enough people notice it, and word of mouth isn't guaranteed. But Denkiworks has decided that useful platform support beats waiting endlessly for a perfect date.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major revision, Luna 4.
  • Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three newly introduced playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.
  • Recent findings suggest that the first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major revision, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of new content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three newly introduced playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

Recent findings suggest that the first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Industry observers note that luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a newly introduced outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This morning, Nintendo shared some updates related to the Pikmin franchise and has officially claimed November 1 as Pikmin Day, starting today and moving forward presumably forever.

In a recent development, aside from the announcement of Pikmin Day as a general idea, Pikmin creator Shigeru Miyamoto appeared on camera to remind everyone that Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy is coming November 12. A free demo for the game, which will include one standard level and two Dandori Academy levels, will be available on November 2.

Industry observers note that the Switch 2 version of the game (you can read Game Informer’s Pikmin 4 review here) will have improved visuals and take advantage of the Switch 2’s mic to let you say things like “Rush” and “Go to work” to Oatchi. The Dandori Academy side of the game is essentially time trials you can practice, and then on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, you will have one chance to post your best time. You can read more about the Switch 2 version of the game here.

Recent findings suggest that miyamoto also shared that the mobile game, Pikmin Bloom, is also getting a fairly substantial update soon with secret caves. In Bloom, players will be able to find maps that reveal caves that you can send your Pikmin into to battle and find treasure. You can also find maps for Bloom by playing Pikmin 4. Caves will be coming to Pikmin Bloom later this year.

The Pikmin Day presentation also reminded viewers that every Pikmin game is available on Switch and Switch 2, though no announcements or hints were made implying that Pikmin 1 and 2 would be coming to the Nintendo Switch Online subscription service, which includes GameCube games on Switch 2. Those games can be purchased individually on the eShop.

According to recent reports, finally, Miyamoto brought actress Fuka Koshiba on the presentation (best known for voicing Kiki in Kiki’s Delivery Service) to share her appreciation for the Pikmin franchise (she likes to knit Pikmin hats that she shares on social media) and introduce a Pikmin short film. In the short, a Pikmin interacts with a toad, but I won’t spoil what happens. Miyamoto promised more shorts are on the way and in the future, they will be found in the Nintendo Today app.

Unfortunately, the stream concluded without a single reference to 2017's Hey! Pikmin. I wouldn't expect it to get a port to Switch 2 anytime soon.

IONNA enables Plug & Charge for Tesla, opens 22 bay site in Westminster, CA

💡 Key Takeaways
  • IONNA, the DC charging operator backed by several major OEMs, has opened its largest DC charging site yet, with 22 bays of 400kW charging in Westminster, California.
  • Alongside the opening, IONNA is also enabling Plug & Charge operation for Tesla EVs, with Stellantis EVs “coming soon.”.
  • IONNA is a rapidly expanding DC charging network which is garnering good reviews from EV drivers, with clean, fast and easy to use charging stations (which it calls “Rechargeries”).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

IONNA, the DC charging operator backed by several major OEMs, has opened its largest DC charging site yet, with 22 bays of 400kW charging in Westminster, California.

Alongside the opening, IONNA is also enabling Plug & Charge operation for Tesla EVs, with Stellantis EVs “coming soon.”.

IONNA is a rapidly expanding DC charging network which is garnering good reviews from EV drivers, with clean, fast and easy to use charging stations (which it calls “Rechargeries”).

But until now, we haven’t had all that many chargers in the LA area. There are a couple in South OC and the Inland Empire, but nothing closer to the population center of the metro area (though more are opening soon).

That changes now with IONNA’s upcoming flagship charging station in Westminster. It features 12 CCS connectors and 10 NACS ports, so you can charge just about any EV (no Chademo, nor can my AC-only Tesla Roadster charge here… ho hum).

In addition to 22 chargers with peak 400kW capacity, the site features indoor and outdoor lounge space, restrooms, and other amenities like an In N Out and a taco shop across the street. (Not quite as full-featured as my favorite charging station, Rove, but IONNA has a much larger national footprint, and does have faster chargers).

It has been revealed that there’s also a small, convenience-store-like area that uses Amazon’s “just walk out” technology. You swipe a card to unlock the room, pick up any items you want, and just walk out. The many cameras on the ceiling track you (and whoever came in with you) and what you’re picking up, then charge your card for the items you took with you.

The store has snacks and drinks, though no ice cream, which is the main thing I’m looking for on a roadtrip stop… IONNA may convert one of the fridges to a freezer in the future, depending on how things go.

And, importantly, the site has trash cans and window wipers – just what you need on a roadtrip stop.

Speaking of roadtrips, the charger opening caps off a cross-country roadtrip by IONNA personnel, who set out in several cars from various parts of the country, all convening on the upcoming Rechargery in Westminster.

According to recent reports, over 20 EVs joined the roadtrip and drove over 40,000 combined miles on their trip to Westminster. The teams charged at approximately 30% of the company’s charging sites, showing just how easy it is to do roadtrips in an EV.

Recent findings suggest that the Rechargery opens tomorrow in Westminster, at 6260 Westminster Blvd, just off the 405 freeway. Look for the big sign. For the first weeks, you can charge at a promotional rate of $0.20/kWh. Afterwards, IONNA will charge its standard rate of $0.39/kWh.

Perhaps more importantly than a latest charger opening, though, is IONNA’s announcement today that Teslas can now use its network with Plug & Charge functionality (well, technically Autocharge, which is basically the same thing).

According to recent reports, awesome!! Since there's none close to my home in Torrance (CA), this is great news. A few months ago, a friend was taking me and the kids to San Diego area when we purchased the 2017 Ford Focus EV and he was driving his Cadillac Optiq. A little further south, we came upon a brand fresh Ionna at Mission Viejo. However, that one wasn't quite open yet. This one is much closer to where I live. I am so happy to see more Ionna's coming soon.

Similarly, just down the street from my house is a site that will be a newly introduced Rove charging place. I don't think they have broken ground yet, so it will be a while. But this one will have a car wash, a little store, Wifi and waiting area and it already has a Chik-fil-a and Panera and Shake Shack. Looking forward to that one as well and it's next to the 405 Freeway.

What this means is that you can link your car and credit card ahead of time (via the Presto charging app), then simply plug in at any IONNA station and start charging, without having to tap or swipe or open an app. This is similar to the experience Teslas have always had on Superchargers, so should be familiar to Tesla owners.

It has been revealed that the functionality is rolled out across all of IONNA’s network, starting today. So you should be able to test it out on your Tesla vehicle. IONNA already supports Plug & Charge for BMW, GM, Hyundai, Kia, Mercedes-Benz, Toyota, Rivian, Ford, Porsche and Volvo EVs.

In a recent development, further, IONNA says support is “coming soon” for Stellantis EVs (Jeep, Dodge, Ram, Fiat), stating that those cars will be able to Plug & Charge on its network in December. It now supports Autocharge for about two thirds of the EVs on American roads.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When the mid-engine C111 sports-car concept made its debut at the Frankfurt auto show in 1969, would-be buyers sent blank checks to Mercedes-Benz headquarters. Despite the fervent interest, however, the C111 never went into production, although a handful of prototypes were built over the years. Now Mercedes-Benz has confirmed that it will auction off one of those cars, making it (at long last) the first C111 to reach private hands. And would-be buyers who wish to take home the C111 will need to muster that same blank-check energy.

See all results for used Mercedes-Benz for sale near 60629.

The C111 was conceived as the modern-day successor to the W198 300SL Gullwing of the 1950s. The two-seat supercar featured a mid-mounted rotary engine, a fiberglass body, and gullwing doors. The following year, an evolved C111-II was unveiled at the 1970 Geneva auto show with a 345-hp 2.4-liter four-rotor engine. The 1973 global oil embargo and the costs to meet rising emissions standards caused the company to shelve the plan for series production, although several more C111 prototypes were made, including a C111-II-D with a diesel engine in 1976 and a diesel-powered C111-III in 1978. A total of 17 cars were made; 13 still exist. Mercedes has kept them all, until now.

Sources indicate that the car being sold is a C111-II built in August 1970. It’s fitted with a 2.4-liter rotary engine making 345 horsepower at 7700 rpm, a five-speed manual transmission, anti-lock brakes, twin fuel tanks, and a Becker Europa radio. Weighing 2734 pounds, the C111-II had a claimed top speed of 186 mph and a 0-to-60-mph time of 4.8 seconds. It was used as a test car, including at the Hockenheimring.

It has been revealed that like most of the C111s, this car is painted Weissherbst orange; the seats are upholstered in houndstooth fabric. The car sits on modern 8-x-15-inch alloy wheels; the original magnesium wheels from 1970 are included, but with the caveat that they “are now suitable only for display purposes.” The anti-lock brake system is not functional.

Sources indicate that the car has been on display at the Mercedes-Benz Museum since 2006. It was sympathetically restored in 2024 in preparation for an appearance at Pebble Beach. The odometer shows 24,766 km (15,389 miles).

In a recent development, the car is being auctioned by RM Sotheby’s this coming February in Paris. The proceeds of the sale will help fund the museum, including an initiative to digitize its contents, part of the “Mercedes-Benz Museum 2.0” project.

See all results for used Mercedes-Benz for sale near 60629.

According to recent reports, to reassure the future buyer that the value of their C111 won’t be diluted by additional examples coming onto the market, Mercedes-Benz has committed to a 25-year moratorium on any future sales of the remaining cars. Mercedes-Benz collectors, call your bankers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, who needs the electric M3 when the regular BMW i3 can already dominate at the track? In this new video from Misha Charoudin, the BMW i3 50 takes to the Nurburgring and not only makes it around the Green Hell without issue, it actually beats up on other performance cars.

The BMW i3 50 xDrive is presently the only variant on sale, and while it isn't a full-blown M car, it has the specs to rival most of the real ones. Its dual motors combine for 463 horsepower and 476 lb-ft of torque, making it more powerful than most M3s throughout history. Those motors get fed electrons by a 109 kWh battery, which is far bigger than most electric sedans of its size. Such a major battery might seem like overkill in an i3, especially since its heft might not seem useful on track. However, that massive pack actually helped it at the 'Ring.

It has been revealed that when Charoudin started the lap, he had 79% state-of-charge (SoC). When he finished the 12-mile lap as hard as he could, he had 65%. A 14% drop after pushing the i3 hard on the most difficult track in the world is pretty dang good. Even more impressive is that, after three more laps with someone else at the helm, it still had 20% battery. Depending on where that i3 calls home, it could have been driven back after four flat-out laps. That's pretty remarkable, especially considering this is just the normal i3.

What's most impressive, though, is how the i3 50 handled the Nurburgring itself. On a normal day, the 'Ring is clogged up by countless sports cars, and even boring rental cars, so unless you're properly quick, you can get caught behind a train of cars. But not the i3. It carved through the traffic with ease, overtook even some serious performance machines, and looked like the fastest car on the track at times.

Recent findings suggest that during the lap, you can see its sharp turn in, explosive power, and strong braking, both regenerative and friction. What's more, it did all of that on eco-friendly EV tires in the cold. So imagine what one could do on a set of stickier summer tires in good temps. The battery didn't even overheat, with the temp gauge saying "OK" until the very last minute. It did eventually say the battery temps got high, but the lap was basically done by that point.

This is the same BMW i3 50 that gets 468 miles of EPA-rated range and drove from Norway to Spain while only charging for a total of two hours and 46 minutes. If it can smoke performance cars at the Nurburgring, can you imagine what the M3 will be like?

Fang Cheng Bao, or FCB as many call it, is another BYD sub-brand, alongside Denza and Yangwang.

BYD has not revealed battery or powertrain specs, but the Ti 6 (Tai 6) is expected to be offered in pure electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) variants.

It will likely offer a similar setup to the Ti 7. The Ti 7 PHEV uses a 1.5L engine and an electric motor that delivers a combined 360 kW (482 hp).

The pure electric version with a single motor delivers 300 kW (402 hp), while the dual-motor variant delivers 515 kW (690 hp).

Since the Tai 7 (Ti 7) starts at 179,800 yuan ($27,000), the smaller Tai 6 (Ti 6) will likely be priced in the 150,00 yuan ($22,500) range.

Lamborghini Temerario Spyder Delivers Open-Air Access to Its 10,000-RPM V-8

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lamborghini has its product development schedule finely tuned.
  • Recent findings suggest that formally introduced Thursday morning at the Academy Museum or Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, the Temerario Spyder isn’t surprising, but it’s still stunning.
  • Sources indicate that the folding solid top itself was co-developed by Germany’s Webasto, the venerable firm that’s also behind folding top modules from the Mazda MX-5 Miata RF to the Ferrari California.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lamborghini has its product development schedule finely tuned. Of course, there was a convertible version of the Temerario coming. And on Wednesday, November 18, the automaker unveiled it for the first time—and it is called, of course, the Temerario Spyder.

Recent findings suggest that formally introduced Thursday morning at the Academy Museum or Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, the Temerario Spyder isn’t surprising, but it’s still stunning. The Temerario was designed with the Spyder always in mind; as such, there’s space enough behind the two seats for the new power folding hardtop to snick down inside almost perfectly vertically. The firewall between the cockpit and the mid-mounted, twin-turbocharged V-8 doesn’t change its location, but the space behind the seats is utilized differently.

Sources indicate that the folding solid top itself was co-developed by Germany’s Webasto, the venerable firm that’s also behind folding top modules from the Mazda MX-5 Miata RF to the Ferrari California. This is the first Lambo to use a retractable hardtop.

Sources indicate that 10 electric actuators split the two-piece top, open a hatch behind the seats, and move the structure down into its narrow warren. It’s a fully electric system, so there are no hydraulic lines to split open. Lamborghini indicates the power top adds about 100 kilograms (220 pounds) to the Temerario’s mass, but that’s all at the center of the car, so that front-to-rear weight balance is maintained. With the roof open, says the maker, the center of gravity drops about three millimeters from where it is when closed.

The hardtop should also produce close to a coupe-like experience when it is closed.“We reinforce the structure of the Spyder,” explains Fermin Soneira, Lambo’s chief technical officer, about the Temerario Spyder’s aluminum space frame. “So, for example, we use some hydroformed pieces in place of castings at some points.”.

The Temerario Spyder takes the market position that was once held by the Huracan Spyder, and Lamborghini claims this new architecture is six percent stiffer in torsional rigidity and nine percent up in dynamic bending stiffness than that car. If all that stiff isn’t stiffy enough, there’s also a six percent increase in dynamic torsional rigidity. So, it’s a super-stiffy thing.

The increase in weight means the suspension has been slightly tweaked to deal with it. “If you change the weight, you have to change the spring rate to keep the same natural frequency,” says Soneira. “In this case, it was not about leaving everything the same, but also about increasing comfort in the ‘Strada’ drive mode. Still, if you go to the Hockenheimring, there’s less than a one second per lap difference between the coupe and the Spyder.”.

Industry observers note that top up or down, the most spectacular element of every Temerario is the flat-plane crank, 4.0-liter twin-turbo V-8 that’s incorporated into the hybrid all-wheel drive powertrain. With a lightweight reciprocating assembly that includes titanium connecting rods, the engine will spin to a thrilling 10,000-rpm redline. “We have a fresh calibration of the engine sound,” adds Soneira, “so you end up with a slightly different voice than in the coupe. The target is always ‘let’s keep improving,’ so these changes will come to the coupe too.”.

Combined with three electric motors, the Temerario has 907 horsepower aboard—and despite all the electronic hickey-doos, it still stirs up and blasts like a true supercar. That’s not likely to change with the Spyder.

Production of the Spyder will be done in batches along the regular Temerario assembly line, with the first saleable models due to be completed as this is published. Lamborghini expects about 50 percent of Temerario production to be Spyders. Prices haven’t been announced, but should start around $400,000 and go up from there only limited by the buyer’s imagination and wallet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Another year is coming to an end, and (as you and I have gotten used to by now) there’s still no Half-Life 3 in sight. You’d think that 22 years after the release of Half-Life 2, it would hurt any less, but nope.

In a bid to soothe aching hearts and Gordon Freeman enthusiasts all around the world, the wizards over at Crowbar Collective have put out a new enhancement to Black Mesa, making the 2020 love letter to Half-Life look better than ever.

In a recent development, this revision, branded a ‘red letter day’ by the developers, focuses first and foremost on visual improvements. Crowbar Collective has managed to make the game look better, while also significantly improving its performance in the process.

In a showcase by the developers, scenes previously clocking around 130 FPS now reach 170 FPS. It’s not clear how these improvements will scale on different hardware, but expect to see noticeable changes across the board.

Industry observers note that on the eyecandy side of things, interiors have now been updated to use parallax-corrected cubemaps (PCC). This technique turns static reflections into dynamic ones by adjusting them based on the player’s perspective. As a result, it adds a lot of depth to interiors while not incurring costs on the performance side. Translucent materials like glass have also been updated to have light behave realistically as it passes through.

Another year is coming to an end, and (as you and I have gotten used to by now) there’s still no Half-Life 3 in sight.

Recent findings suggest that while interiors got plenty of jazz, there have also been major improvements to the game’s environmental lighting as a whole. Crowbar Collective has improved the Source Engine’s light bouncing, making indirect illumination behave more realistically. Outdoor scenes have received image-based lighting, using HDR to bring more accurate outputs.

As a love letter to Valve’s magnum opus, it’s only natural for Black Mesa to cater to the company’s handheld console. Following the revision’s performance improvements, Black Mesa has received the Steam Deck Verified badge.

It has been revealed that the latest enhancement to Black Mesa has modernized the user interface to make it behave better with stick controls, benefiting both Steam Deck and PC owners who play with controllers. According to Crowbar Collective, keyboard and mouse have also been refined. Nostalgics can still pick the classic Half-Life menu from the Steam Workshop.

The popular Blue Shift mod by HECU Collective, which tells the game’s story through the eyes of Barney Calhoun, has been updated to be compatible with the latest version of Black Mesa.

For now, this massive patch to Black Mesa is all we have until the yearly ritual of hoping for a Half-Life 3 reveal at The Game Awards. Earlier this year, Valve composer Mike Morasky alluded to a certain game codenamed ‘HLX’, which some of the more hopeful types have taken to be a working title for the much anticipated sequel.

Industry observers note that that is not the first time Morasky has run his mouth about the HLX project, so maybe, just maybe, this time it’s for real. Until more evidence surfaces, you’ll find me playing Black Mesa.

Black Mesa is available via Windows and Linux platforms via Steam.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (426 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Electrek

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Toyota is recalling 19,000 electric C-HR SUVs globally, with about 10,000 affected in the US.
  • In September, Toyota issued a safety recall involving certain model-year 2026 C-HR electric SUVs in North America.
  • Toyota initially said about 10,000 models were involved, but later confirmed the number was 8,521 in a letter to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota is recalling 19,000 electric C-HR SUVs globally, with about 10,000 affected in the US.

In September, Toyota issued a safety recall involving certain model-year 2026 C-HR electric SUVs in North America.

Toyota initially said about 10,000 models were involved, but later confirmed the number was 8,521 in a letter to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).

It has been revealed that according to Germany’s federal motor authority, Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA), the recall has now expanded to 19,000 C-HR vehicles globally. In Germany, the recall impacts 1,096 vehicles and is still under investigation by the KBA.

The problem stems from faulty software programming in the EV-ECU. While it’s intended to limit the battery’s charge level, the software can cause it to overcharge under certain conditions.

Toyota said the issue occurs if the battery is already at a high state of charge and the driver continues using the regenerative braking system.

When this happens, warning lights and a sound will alert the driver, and the electric drive system can shut down, causing the vehicle to lose power while driving.

Following an internal investigation, Toyota mentioned in the NHTSA report that the issue was caused by incorrect software that disrupted the charging-limit function, allowing the battery to overcharge while driving.

The Toyota C-HR vehicles included in the recall were produced between June 17, 2025, and July 9, 2026.

In Europe and other overseas markets, Toyota sells the C-HR EV as the C-HR+ to distinguish it from the gas- or hybrid-powered version.

Owners of affected vehicles in North America can take them to a Toyota dealership, where the battery ECU software will be updated free of charge.

Recent findings suggest that toyota mailed owner notification letters out on October 18, 2026. Owners can contact Toyota’s customer service at 1-800-331-4331. The recall number is 26TA17.

Other than saying the EV-ECU is being reprogrammed, Toyota has not yet unveiled next steps for owners of affected vehicles outside North America. The KBA reference number is 17116R.

Check back for more details. The recall only affects the 2026 C-HR. The 2027 Toyota C-HR is also now on sale.

The upcoming BMW M3 EV sports sedan represents BMW's biggest attempt to woo electric-car buyers to date. The maker's first inception-to-showroom production electric M car carries styling derived from the standard i3, but with M-specific fender bulges, aero enhancements, and racier-looking exterior lighting elements. BMW says the M3 EV will coexist with a gasoline-powered M3, which should arrive in showrooms ahead of the electric model.

Industry observers note that like the i3 and BMW's other Neue Klasse models, the M3 EV features an 800-volt architecture and batteries that offer 20 percent higher energy density than past EVs. BMW M vehicles have cultivated a devoted following for their sublime performance, and it stands to reason that BMW wouldn't risk tainting that legacy when the power comes from electrons instead of gasoline.

Expert Tip: If you can't wait for the M3 EV to launch before deciding on your next BMW sports sedan, consider the outgoing i4, which is one of our favorite EVs and can be had with a 592-hp dual-motor powertrain.

Recent findings suggest that everything. Details are scarce, but we know the M3 will ride atop BMW's fresh EV platform. Production is expected to begin sometime in 2027.

Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.

The M3 EV will be powered by four electric motors producing a total of 838 horsepower and 885 pound-feet of torque. The motors themselves are of the electrically excited variety, and the quad-motor setup allows for torque vectoring both front to back and side to side. The car operates in rear-wheel-drive mode most of the time, with the front motors coming online when needed.

Industry observers note that the M3 EV utilizes BMW's "Heart of Joy" control unit and software, which handles the drivetrain, braking, charging, regeneration, and steering functions. When we drove a prototype of the electric M3, we found it to be a beast on the racetrack. We also experimented with the different drive modes, including the fake gearshifts and sounds in the various eDrive settings, but thought the car was best in Auto mode.

Recent findings suggest that BMW says the electric M3 will come with a battery pack measuring roughly 100 kilowatt-hours. This should provide an EPA-rated driving range of around 300 miles, though we’re still awaiting official EPA estimates. DC fast-charging capability is remarked to be up to 420 kilowatts, which should enable the M3 to add a considerable amount of range in a short period of time.

It has been revealed that first Row: Like the i3, the M3 EV features BMW's latest digital dashboard, which features a trapezoidal infotainment display. The concept car pictured here shows deeply bucketed performance seats with five-point safety harnesses, but expect normal chairs and seatbelts on the production model. The concept vehicle also showed a cloth trim piece on the dashboard with multi-colored ambient backlighting.

Second Row: A pair of bucket seats was shown in the concept vehicle, although we think a three-across bench will at least be offered on the production M3 EV.

Cargo Capacity: We aren't sure about the M3 EV's cargo capacity yet, but we expect to see storage in both the trunk and the front trunk.

The touchscreen offers a high level of customization and features a matrix backlight for easy visibility in all conditions. BMW's fresh Panoramic Vision system projects crucial information onto the lower part of the windshield, stretching from A-pillar to A-pillar. Logically, key driving information is displayed on the left for the driver, while central and right-hand areas of the display can be personalized and are visible to all occupants.

Recent findings suggest that up to six widgets can be moved from the infotainment screen to the Panoramic Vision system by drag and drop, and further customization of both screens can be manipulated by buttons on the steering wheel. A head-up display is available, and smartphones and smartwatches from all leading manufacturers can be programmed to operate as the vehicle key.

  • Musk revealed the strategy at the Latest York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, noting that Tesla wants to take the basic premise of what it can offer with the Cybercab—a fully autonomous vehicle that can operate as a managed fleet car—to a platform that can seat more than just two people.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that tesla has already built one model without a steering wheel or pedals. But one was not enough, and CEO Elon Musk is eyeing another model for an autonomous upgrade.

Musk said Wednesday that Tesla will build a steering-wheel-free, fully autonomous version of the Model Y.

Musk revealed the strategy at the Latest York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, noting that Tesla wants to take the basic premise of what it can offer with the Cybercab—a fully autonomous vehicle that can operate as a managed fleet car—to a platform that can seat more than just two people.

"It's going to make sense for us to make cars that can seat different amounts of people,” said Musk. “We still need autonomous vehicles if you've got four or six, or a whole family. What we plan to do is have an autonomous version of the Model Y that won't have steering wheels or pedals and would be good for transporting groups of six or seven people.".

Now, before getting too far—yes, you’re still going to be able to order a regular-size Model Y with a steering wheel for the foreseeable future. But Tesla wants a robotaxi that can accommodate an actual family.

Tesla already uses the Model Y in its autonomous fleet. However, those cars retain the basic driving controls that Tesla now wants to eliminate in its fully autonomous variant. Musk’s proposed version would seemingly delete them from the factory and create a larger autonomous car that passengers could ride in, but not drive—similar to the Cybercab.

To Musk’s point, Cybercab is intentionally tiny. Its two-seat configuration “covers 90% of all passenger miles,” according to Musk. That means that Tesla can cut down on production costs by reducing the interior complexity in order to make the Cybercab cost under $30,000.

Industry observers note that musk didn’t say when (or if) this variant would be offered to the public to purchase. The Cybercab only recently became available for hand-picked private buyers to purchase, and even then, there are a number of asterisks involved (like where the car can operate, and the mandatory $300 per month autonomy subscription required for the car to move).

Industry observers note that nevertheless, if Tesla is going to build driverless cars, an autonomous Model Y makes sense if Tesla can keep costs down and safely deploy it in enough usable areas. But with a $300 per month cost on top of the vehicle, would Tesla’s ideal audience be fleet operators or private buyers?

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The US has installed more than 200 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery storage, with nearly 50 GWh coming online in the first nine months of 2026 alone.
  • It has been revealed that the US added 48.3 GWh of battery storage through September, up 20% from the same stretch last year, according to the latest report from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence.
  • Texas added 12.3 GWh of grid-scale batteries through September, more than any other state.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The US has installed more than 200 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery storage, with nearly 50 GWh coming online in the first nine months of 2026 alone.

It has been revealed that the US added 48.3 GWh of battery storage through September, up 20% from the same stretch last year, according to the latest report from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. Q3 was a little slower: The US installed 14.3 GWh in those three months, down 1% year over year.

Texas added 12.3 GWh of grid-scale batteries through September, more than any other state. Arizona came in second at 7.7 GWh, followed by California at 6.8 GWh. And 11 states had already broken their annual storage installation records with three months to go – Colorado, Massachusetts, Utah, Michigan, Georgia, Mississippi, Virginia, Iowa, Montana, Alabama, and Illinois.

Utility-scale batteries did most of the work in Q3, accounting for 12.2 GWh of fresh capacity. Businesses and industrial sites added another 1.3 GWh, and residential added 746 megawatt-hours (MWh). That was the best Q3 yet for home batteries, though installs through September were still down 12% year over year. Some homeowners moved up their installations last year before the federal residential clean energy tax credit ended.

“States are moving from targets to centralized procurements,” remarked Pete Tillotson, a senior analyst at Benchmark. In September, Latest York awarded contracts for eight battery projects that can deliver about 950 megawatts (MW) combined. SEIA and Benchmark now expect 708 GWh of storage across the grid, homes, and businesses by 2030, up 3.7% from their previous forecast.

The US can also make more battery cells here. A Tennessee factory opened in July and an Indiana factory opened in October, bringing US cell manufacturing capacity to 92.4 GWh, up 50%.

Solar and batteries helped bring down average summer wholesale power prices by 42% in Texas’s ERCOT market and 51% in California’s CAISO market between 2021 and 2026, according to SEIA’s inflation-adjusted analysis. When batteries had power to spare during peak hours, grid operators could call on expensive power plants less often.

You wouldn’t know it from looking at the total on residential electric bills. The cost of generating power for households fell in both markets, but the cost of delivering it to homes rose. Overall, residential bills rose 22% at the two California utilities SEIA examined and 3% across its Texas utility sample, driven by higher transmission and distribution costs. California is upgrading its grid to reduce the risk of wildfires. Texas is expanding its grid for rising demand and make it more resilient to storms.

It has been revealed that the article is good with the reporting about grid tied storage, but seems to miss the forest for the trees with it comes to pricing. Texas isn't installing more grid tied storage because of altruistic intent.

It has been revealed that the storage is being added because they electricity suppliers can use it to make money. They can make money because we have a reasonably well thought out wholesale electrical market AND because that market has purchases large amounts of solar and wind generation.

That combination means that I still pay just $0.01 more per kwh than I did when I moved to this state 20 years ago. I pay 12 cents per kwh and Texas average is between 12 and 15. A functional market is what makes that work.

More than 300 solar and battery storage companies in the US wrote to Congress last week asking it to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. SEIA CEO Tim Pawlenty indicates the permitting bill would help get projects built faster and ease pressure on power prices. However, many Democrats feel this bill falls short. The Senate voted 70–27 on Monday to end debate on the amendment containing the bill’s text, moving it closer to a final vote.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

In a recent development, as recently revealed, the latest experience rolls out today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the strategy is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as swiftly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

According to recent reports, the Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two fresh additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alpitronic, the tech giant that makes the DC fast chargers used by Ionna, Walmart, Mercedes-Benz, BP Pulse, and others, is building a new factory in the United States that will boost output of its 400- and 1,000-kilowatt stalls.

The manufacturer’s newly introduced 173,315-square-foot facility, located in Fort Mill, South Carolina, will create 70 new jobs and will also act as a testing lab, repair center, logistics hub, and warehouse.

Alpitronic, which has its North American headquarters in Charlotte, North Carolina, and its global headquarters in Bolzano, Italy, noted it will invest $33.94 million in the new facility, with $200,000 coming from York County’s Coordinating Council for Economic Development in the form of a Set-Aside grant to assist with the costs of building improvements.

“North America is central to our next phase of growth, and investing in our manufacturing capabilities is key to supporting that expansion,” said Patrik Herrnegger, Alpitronic Americas CEO. “Our Fort Mill facility will put U.S. production under our direct control, bringing us closer to our customers and enabling us to serve them more efficiently. We thank South Carolina and York County for their partnership as we prepare to begin production in early 2027.”.

Back in 2024, the company worked with a third-party production partner to open its first local manufacturing facility in Wisconsin. Now, manufacturing has moved in-house, with Alpitronic wholly owning the production operation.

Sources indicate that the newly introduced South Carolina plant will assemble HYC400 and HYC1000 stalls, Alpitronic stated. The HYC400 all-in-one dispensers can deliver up to 400 kW of power to a single connected electric vehicle without needing a separate power cabinet, and are the current charger of choice for Ionna and Walmart.

The higher-powered HYC1000 system is composed of a 1,000-kW power cabinet and up to four stalls that can deliver up to 600 kW to a single EV. Each stall can have two ports, and the system can dynamically allocate power to each vehicle to make the best use of the available power.

What makes the organization's dispensers different from most competitors is the use of silicon carbide components, which lower energy losses and, subsequently, the amount of money EV drivers have to pay for a top-up. According to Alpitronic, SiC modules enable 97.5% efficiency and allow for smaller, quieter, and cooler stalls.

Alpitronic’s newly introduced factory in Fort Mill, South Carolina, is scheduled to go online in February 2027.
