Wine, beer, or spirits? Massive study reveals a surprising health divide

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1529 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A massive study involving more than 340,000 adults has uncovered a surprising difference in the health risks associated with wine, beer, cider, and spirits.
  • According to recent reports, researchers found that low to moderate wine consumption was associated with a lower risk of death, particularly from cardiovascular disease.
  • It has been revealed that the results also reinforce a broader conclusion from previous research: drinking less alcohol is generally better for health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A massive study involving more than 340,000 adults has uncovered a surprising difference in the health risks associated with wine, beer, cider, and spirits. Although heavy drinking was linked to worse health outcomes regardless of the beverage, the picture was more complicated among people who consumed smaller amounts of alcohol.

According to recent reports, researchers found that low to moderate wine consumption was associated with a lower risk of death, particularly from cardiovascular disease. In contrast, similar amounts of beer, cider, and spirits were linked to a higher risk. The findings, presented at the American College of Cardiology's Annual Scientific Session (ACC.26), suggest that both the type and quantity of alcohol may influence its relationship with long-term health.

It has been revealed that the results also reinforce a broader conclusion from previous research: drinking less alcohol is generally better for health. Importantly, the new findings do not establish that wine itself protects against disease.

"These results come from the general population, and in certain high-risk groups, such as people with chronic diseases or cardiovascular conditions, the risks could be even higher," said Zhangling Chen, MD, PhD, a professor at the Second Xiangya Hospital, Central South University in China and the study's senior author.

How a Study of 340,000 Adults Measured Alcohol Risk.

Industry observers note that to investigate the relationship between drinking habits and longevity, scientists examined data from 340,924 adults enrolled in the UK Biobank between 2006 and 2022. The UK Biobank is a large research resource that collects health and lifestyle information to help scientists investigate factors associated with disease and mortality.

It has been revealed that participants reported their alcohol consumption through dietary questionnaires when they joined the study. Researchers then classified them into four groups based on how much pure alcohol they typically consumed each day or week, rather than simply counting drinks.

Recent findings suggest that this distinction matters because beer, wine, and spirits contain different concentrations of alcohol. For comparison, a 12-ounce can of beer, a 5-ounce glass of wine, and a 1.5-ounce shot of spirits each provide approximately 14 grams of pure alcohol.

In a recent development, people consuming fewer than 20 g (about 1.5 standard drinks) per week were placed in the never or occasional drinking group. Low consumption was defined as 20 g per week up to 20 g per day for men, and 20 g per week up to 10 g per day for women.

Sources indicate that moderate drinking was defined as 20 g to 40 g (about 1.5 to three standard drinks) daily for men and 10 g to 20 g daily for women. High consumption meant more than 40 g (about three drinks) per day for men or more than 20 g (about 1.5 drinks) per day for women.

Researchers followed participants' health outcomes for an average of more than 13 years, allowing them to examine how drinking patterns were associated with deaths from different causes.

Wine, Beer, and Spirits Show Different Heart Health Risks.

Industry observers note that the clearest finding concerned heavy alcohol consumption. Compared with people who never drank or consumed alcohol only occasionally, heavy drinkers had a 24% higher risk of dying from any cause. Their risk of dying from cancer was 36% higher, while their risk of dying from heart disease was 14% higher.

These increased risks were associated with heavy drinking regardless of whether participants preferred wine, beer, cider, or spirits.

However, the results became more surprising when researchers examined low and moderate alcohol consumption. At these levels, the type of beverage was associated with substantially different outcomes.

People who consumed wine in low to moderate amounts had a significantly lower risk of death, while those who consumed comparable amounts of beer, cider, or spirits had a significantly higher risk.

In a recent development, the contrast was especially striking for cardiovascular disease, a broad category of conditions affecting the heart and blood vessels. Moderate wine drinkers had a 21% lower risk of dying from cardiovascular disease than people who never or only occasionally drank alcohol.

By comparison, even low consumption of beer, cider, or spirits was associated with a 9% higher risk of cardiovascular death.

Sources indicate that these percentages describe relative differences in risk between groups, not the absolute probability that an individual will die from cardiovascular disease. Because the research was observational, the findings also cannot demonstrate that choosing one alcoholic beverage over another directly changes a person's risk.

"Our findings help clarify previously mixed evidence on low to moderate alcohol consumption," Chen remarked. "These findings can help refine guidance, emphasizing that the health risks of alcohol depend not only on the amount of alcohol consumed, but also on the type of beverage. Even low to moderate intake of spirits, beer, or cider is linked to higher mortality, while low to moderate intake of wine may carry lower risk.".

Why Might Wine Be Linked to Lower Heart Risks?

Researchers identified several possible explanations for the differences, including the chemical composition of wine and the habits of people who drink it.

Red wine contains polyphenols, naturally occurring compounds found in plants that can have antioxidant properties. Antioxidants help counter certain chemical reactions involving unstable molecules that can damage cells. Some polyphenols have been investigated for potential benefits to blood vessels and cardiovascular function.

These compounds could contribute to the associations observed in wine drinkers, although the study did not establish that they were responsible for the lower mortality risk.

Another possible explanation involves how and when people drink.

Sources indicate that wine is more commonly consumed alongside meals, and wine drinkers often report healthier diets and lifestyle habits. Drinking wine may therefore be associated with other behaviors that support cardiovascular health.

According to recent reports, beer, cider, and spirits, on the other hand, are more frequently consumed outside of meals. In this study, people who favored these beverages also tended to have poorer overall diet quality and other lifestyle factors associated with increased health risks.

Such differences make it difficult to separate the effects of the alcohol itself from the characteristics and habits of the people consuming it.

"Taken together, these factors suggest that the type of alcohol, how it is consumed, and the associated lifestyle behaviors all contribute to the observed differences in mortality risk," Chen stated.

What the Findings Mean for Alcohol and Health.

In a recent development, to make their comparisons more reliable, the researchers statistically adjusted their analyses for numerous factors that might influence mortality. These included age and other demographic characteristics, socioeconomic circumstances, lifestyle behaviors, and cardiometabolic health.

Sources indicate that cardiometabolic factors include conditions and measurements related to heart and metabolic health, such as blood pressure, blood sugar regulation, and cholesterol levels. The analyses also accounted for family histories of diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and cancer.

Even with these adjustments, the researchers emphasized several key limitations.

Sources indicate that because the study was observational, it could identify associations between alcohol consumption and mortality but could not prove that particular beverages caused better or worse outcomes. Other differences between participants may have influenced the findings despite the statistical adjustments.

Alcohol intake was also measured through questionnaires completed when participants first entered the study. That information depended on participants accurately reporting their own drinking habits, and it did not capture changes in consumption during the years that followed.

Industry observers note that another consideration is that UK Biobank participants tend to be healthier than the general population. This could limit how well the findings apply to other groups of people.

According to recent reports, the researchers suggested that high-quality randomized trials could provide stronger evidence about the health effects of different drinking patterns. Such studies would help clarify whether the observed differences reflect the beverages themselves or other factors associated with their consumption.

In a recent development, nevertheless, the enormous study population and more than 13 years of average follow-up provide considerable statistical strength. By examining specific types of alcohol, different levels of consumption, and multiple causes of death, the research offers a more detailed picture of alcohol's potential health risks than many earlier investigations.

The findings highlight an vital distinction: while heavy drinking is consistently associated with harmful health outcomes, the relationships observed at lower consumption levels may depend on beverage choice, drinking habits, and broader lifestyle patterns.

Industry observers note that for now, the apparent advantage among wine drinkers should not be interpreted as a reason to start drinking wine for heart health. The evidence points to a complex relationship between alcohol and mortality, rather than proving that any alcoholic drink offers protection.

Ziyue Li presented the study, "Alcohol Use at Mid-Life and All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality," at ACC.26.

Rockstar President Breaks Silence Ahead of GTA 6 Launch

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Given the mad fervor with which the universe as we know it is preparing for the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 tomorrow, I don’t think it’d be hyperbolic to call Rockstar the, er, rockstar of video game development.
  • Even so, not everyone who works at Rockstar is the kind of person who seeks out the public eye.
  • However, with such a major landmark title like GTA 6 quite literally on the horizon, the president of the firm bringing it is at least informally obligated to share a few words, and that’s exactly what Houser did in a brief, yet poignant statement shared with IGN.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Given the mad fervor with which the universe as we know it is preparing for the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 tomorrow, I don’t think it’d be hyperbolic to call Rockstar the, er, rockstar of video game development. Even if its games take a hot minute to come out, they’re always bangers when they do, and both the industry and the gaming public naturally hang upon their every word in a manner not dissimilar to someone like Mick Jagger.

Even so, not everyone who works at Rockstar is the kind of person who seeks out the public eye. Take, for example, Sam Houser, who is both the president of Rockstar and the executive producer of GTA 6. Houser has worked on the GTA series in some capacity since its very first title in 1997, but unlike some of the firm’s more front-facing divisions and employees, he has always had a tendency to keep his head down and just let the games speak for themselves.

However, with such a major landmark title like GTA 6 quite literally on the horizon, the president of the firm bringing it is at least informally obligated to share a few words, and that’s exactly what Houser did in a brief, yet poignant statement shared with IGN.

Industry observers note that as Houser explained to IGN, the predominant belief that spurs Rockstar’s developmental ethos forward is that games can be just as poignant of a medium of storytelling as any other, whether it be film, television, or print. Not only that, but games, in their ideal form, can become a vital component of the modern cultural zeitgeist and give rise to settings and characters that stick with us long after the fact.

Sources indicate that this firm belief has culminated in the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 after 13 long years of development. “While things have changed and time has passed, one aspect holds true: We have tried to create an experience that will exceed your expectations while showing what this medium is capable of, and why we believe games are so special,” Houser mentioned.

He added that, whether someone is experiencing the GTA series for the first time or has been with it since the very beginning, the game’s world and the narrative contained within it is meant to be shaped by player interaction.

We have tried to create an experience that will exceed your expectations while showing what this medium is capable of.

Recent findings suggest that “We hope it felt both familiar and entirely latest, and above all, we hope that you had fun. We are incredibly grateful to you and everything that you do to celebrate games. We look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with you,” Houser concluded with a word of thanks.

Industry observers note that obviously, every professional game developer out there wants their product to be well-received, both so it makes back the money invested into it, and so that it really sticks with the players who experienced it. Grand Theft Auto 6 may not technically be out yet, but even ahead of release proper, I’d say it’s well on track to meeting and exceeding Houser’s hopes.

For one thing, just this morning, the embargo officially broke on the game’s critical reviews, and perhaps unsurprisingly, GTA 6 has received the official seal of being the hottest thing since toasted bread, both from our own Steve Hannley and pretty much everyone else. Its Metacritic reviewer average has reached 99, tying it with one of the most highly-reviewed games of all time, the original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which is kind of amusing considering the remake of that game just came out.

As for cash, well, it’s difficult to say for certain without hard numbers, but pre-release projections had the game netting its publisher, Take-Two Interactive, a stunning $3.5 billion in revenue, and considering the number of people planning on skipping work to play on launch day, I’d say that’s a fairly realistic figure.

Breaking: Boost and Booster Seats: Comparing the Turbocharged 2026 VW Tiguan and Mazda CX-50

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1935 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Caranddriver

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the horsepower wars are not relegated to machines purpose-built for performance.
  • According to recent reports, of course, building a holistically satisfying family car involves more than just adding power.
  • Both models here—the Tiguan SEL R-Line and the CX-50 Premium Plus—represent the pinnacle of their lineups and are thus quite expensive as far as small family SUVs go.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the horsepower wars are not relegated to machines purpose-built for performance. Nowadays, it feels like nearly every automaker has some sort of higher-output solution available across a surprisingly wide swath of its fleet, including seemingly pedestrian family vehicles. Some might come via electrification, but in the case of the two vehicles before us today—the 2026 Volkswagen Tiguan and 2026 Mazda CX-50—these hi-po conveyances twist the asphalt with good old-fashioned gasoline and turbochargers.

According to recent reports, of course, building a holistically satisfying family car involves more than just adding power. Extra oomph might satisfy the driver, but automakers must pay attention to a whole host of other factors to make things just as peachy for the passengers. Let’s see which of these two compact SUVs does just that.

Both models here—the Tiguan SEL R-Line and the CX-50 Premium Plus—represent the pinnacle of their lineups and are thus quite expensive as far as small family SUVs go. The Tiguan’s lineup starts at $32,280 for the S, and our tester bookends the other side of the offerings at $46,170 as tested. The CX-50 is less expensive, starting at $31,395 for the Select model; our range-topper’s window sticker came in slightly more affordable than the VW’s at $45,210.

See all results for new 2026 Mazda CX-50 for sale near 51503.

Neither of these vehicles is a screaming deal, but you can save a bit of scratch on the VW. Skip our car’s $850 Avocado Green paint, $405 auto-dimming rearview mirror, and $365 in floor mats and bumper protectors, and the price delta evens out. Our Mazda’s Cypress Green paint was only $200 by comparison; all-weather floor mats and a cargo liner added another $390 to its bottom line.

Since both models are the top of their pops, you get a stout list of features. The CX-50’s Premium Plus niceties include a surround-view camera, auto-dimming inside and side-view mirrors, rear automatic braking, and blind-spot monitoring. The Tiguan SEL R-Line takes things a step further with massaging front seats (something Mazda doesn’t offer on any vehicle it sells), plus a more aggressive R-Line appearance package that deletes most of the brightwork around the windows and front fascia.

Industry observers note that looks can be deceiving. The Tiguan’s boxy form may appear larger in all dimensions, but it exceeds the Mazda only in overall width (by nearly four inches, including mirrors) and height (by two to three inches). The CX-50 has about an inch more overall length, wheelbase, and ride height.

Slip inside, and the CX-50 puts more stock in front legroom, where it beats the Tiguan, but the Mazda’s rear passengers must make do with fractionally less gam space. Owing in part to its more upright body shape, the Tiguan takes the cargo-capacity crown, offering better volume whether the rear seats are up or down.

See all results for new 2026 Mazda CX-50 for sale near 51503.

According to recent reports, when it comes to cabin aesthetics, both are swinging for the fences. The CX-50’s white-on-black interior carries plush touch points and premium materials, and we love how many physical buttons, dials, and switches exist across nearly every surface. The tucked-away infotainment screen feels like a vestige of an earlier age, and it sort of is—the CX-50 is due for an update that brings it in line with the latest CX-5, for better or worse (read our latest long-term CX-5 update for more on that).

HIGHS: More guts than the average canopic jar, superb bump suppression, feels fancy.LOWS: Creature-comfort corner cutting, tighter rear-seat accommodations, not a highway-fuel-economy hero.VERDICT: A rocket that could use more pockets.

Industry observers note that the Tiguan’s cabin is also top-notch. Our tester’s two-tone brown and black interior looks and feels no less luxurious than an Audi’s, and we enjoyed the door-to-door strip of wood, which adds some extra variety. Of course, the latest-gen Tiguan is all about the screens, which in this case comprise a normal digital gauge display and a 15-inch repurposed highway billboard. In addition to having more cargo capacity, the Tiguan also has more places to stash your stuff.

We have one weird thing to point out, but it’s bound to be important to somebody. Both cars have heated steering wheels, but the Mazda’s heating element seems confined to between 9 and 10 o’clock on the left and between 2 and 3 o’clock on the right, while the rest of the tiller remains icy to the touch. Volkswagen’s engineers, on the other hand, smartly realized that if you pay for a heated steering wheel, you probably want one that’s warm the whole way around.

Even among high-strung turbo fours, the No Replacement for Displacement adage still holds true. The Mazda CX-50’s 256-hp turbocharged 2.5-liter makes less horsepower than the Tiguan, but the larger mill churns out an absurd 320 pound-feet of torque. All-wheel drive is standard, as is an archaic six-speed automatic transmission. The CX-50 is the lightweight here, tipping the scales at 3864 pounds.

In a recent development, by comparison, the Tiguan’s 2.0-liter turbo four makes just 258 pound-feet of torque, but at 268 horses, it bests the Mazda on raw horsepower. All-wheel drive is standard here as well, and the transmission is a more modern-feeling eight-speed auto. The whole Teutonic shebang carries about one more human’s worth of mass in its structure, weighing 4023 pounds on our scales.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re assuming that the lighter, more torquey SUV will outperform its competition, you’re right, but the gap is small. The last CX-50 we tested hustles to 60 mph in 6.4 seconds—two-tenths ahead of the Tiguan—and the Mazda’s 167-foot stop from 70 mph bests the VW by nine feet. From there, things really tighten up: The CX-50’s 14.9-second, 92-mph quarter-mile sprint is just a hair ahead of the Tiguan’s 15.0 seconds at 96 mph. With a 5-mph rolling start, the two reach 60 within a tenth of each other. From 50 to 70, the Vee-Dub takes the lead, requiring just 4.5 seconds to the Mazda’s 4.8. The Mazda notches a victory around the skidpad, maintaining 0.84 g of lateral grip against the Volkswagen’s 0.78 g.

HIGHS: Posh cabin trimmings, slightly more spacious inside, the most fun we’ve had in a VW SUV in a while.LOWS: Not our favorite infotainment interface, not our favorite brake pedal, traditional German road compliance.VERDICT: Fun for the whole family, driver included.

According to recent reports, unfortunately, the CX-50’s lighter curb weight and slicker-looking silhouette don’t translate to stonkin’ fuel-economy benefits. The two vehicles are nearly evenly matched by EPA estimates—both earned 29-mpg highway and 25-mpg combined ratings, but the Mazda’s 23-mpg city value tops the VW’s by one. The script flipped on our real-world 75-mph highway fuel-economy test, however, where the Tiguan overachieved with a 31-mpg result, out-skinflinting the 28-mpg Mazda, which fell short of its EPA highway estimate.

It has been revealed that both SUVs are fun to drive and reward time spent behind the wheel, with each vehicle carrying its own little idiosyncrasies. There are a few parts of the driving experience where we think the CX-50 shines, and others where the Tiguan feels better.

The Mazda’s cabin may be louder at wide-open throttle (and tied at a 70-mph cruise), but overall, it seems quieter in day-to-day operation, especially over the zydeco washboards that Ann Arbor calls roads. The CX-50’s bump damping is superior, making for a slightly more luxurious ride quality than the Tiguan, which carries some of that stereotypical German stiffness in its suspension tuning—but one person’s “flinty” is another person’s “composed,” so it really boils down to whether you want that additional poise in your daily driving. (The Tiguan SE and base S offer smaller wheels with cushier tire sidewalls.).

When it comes to pedal feel, the Mazda takes the crown; the Tiguan’s brake pedal is a little mushy, and the throttle is a little too eager to open ’er up with a gentle tip-in. On the other hand, we preferred the Volkswagen’s heftier steering feel. The Mazda’s six-speed automatic handles gear changes deftly, but it’s clear from our on-ramp-style acceleration testing that the VW’s two extra gears are, in fact, providing a benefit. (Highway fuel-economy results reflect that as well.) It’s not like you’ll notice either gearbox doing its job, though.

Sources indicate that by the skin of its teeth, the Volkswagen Tiguan claims the championship belt that it lost to the Mazda CX-50 in a 2024 two-car comparo. Back then, we stated the CX-50 was worth the upcharge over the more efficient, more spacious Volkswagen because we preferred the Mazda’s cabin and driving dynamics.

It has been revealed that now, the Tiguan is the one that costs more, and while it remains more efficient and more spacious than the CX-50, it picked up some major slack in the interior-design department, and it drives just about as well. The 2026 Tiguan is an excellent all-rounder. It’s a wonder what a latest generation can do.

  • Recent findings suggest that while the game can be played on PC through TapTap, the developer’s own emulator, many had been anticipating the Steam launch.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Easter Eggs That Did And Did Not Make It Into The 2026 Remake

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (932 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo 64 is a game full of Easter Eggs, secrets, and hidden mechanics (did you know if a butterfly lands on your Deku Stick, it summons a fairy?).
  • Sources indicate that in the courtyard where Link first meets Zelda, there is arguably the most fourth-wall-breaking Easter Egg in the whole game.
  • It has been revealed that for the 2026 remake, there are no references to other Nintendo characters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo 64 is a game full of Easter Eggs, secrets, and hidden mechanics (did you know if a butterfly lands on your Deku Stick, it summons a fairy?). Now in its second remake, not every secret has made its way forward through the previous iterations, but many have. Below you will learn about a few of the secrets that made the cut, and others that didn’t.

Sources indicate that in the courtyard where Link first meets Zelda, there is arguably the most fourth-wall-breaking Easter Egg in the whole game. If you don’t rush to Zelda and instead pause and enter first-person to look around, you will see portraits of other Nintendo characters through the windows, like Mario and Yoshi. In the 3DS remake, the portraits are replaced by an image of a Mario stage.

It has been revealed that for the 2026 remake, there are no references to other Nintendo characters. Instead, the tapestry you build over the course of the game is on display. Removing the reference to Nintendo characters outside of the Zelda universe is understandable, but it is a little odd that art representing the full adventure of the game – an adventure that has not yet concluded – is on the wall.

Industry observers note that as stated above, the Nintendo character portraits are gone, but there is still a guard you can annoy. If you fire a Deku Seed into the left window, a guard will pop out, yell at you, and then throw a bomb at you. You can’t pick up the bomb. In fact, at this point in the game, you haven’t even seen a bomb.

Sources indicate that the Hyrule Castle portrait references to Yoshi and Mario are gone (though Mario and Luigi are still kind of in the game in a way), but Bowser gets a pass for some reason. Both Malon and her dad, Talon, are still wearing Bowser pins on their clothes. And unlike the N64 game where the detail was a little vague, there is no mistaking it here.

Gossip Stones are all over Ocarina of Time and it takes a while to understand what they do. If you hit them with a sword, they tell you the time, and if you play Zelda’s Lullaby near them, they refill your magic. If you do the Happy Mask Salesman’s side quest, interacting with them while wearing the Mask of Truth offers little hints and details about the world. But then there are interactions that are just odd for no reason. Blowing up a bomb near a Gossip Stone still makes it take off like a rocket ship, and using the Megaton Hammer still flattens them for a moment like a Looney Tunes.

And speaking of playing Zelda’s Lullaby for inanimate objects, if you slash a sign to pieces with your sword and regret your words and deeds, you can play the iconic tune to make the signs reform and become readable again.

Recent findings suggest that this detail was exclusive to the 3DS remake of Ocarina of Time, and surprising no one, it has been removed. Ocarina of Time launched in June 2011 and Nintendo released Skyward Sword about five months later in November. For… marketing purposes, I guess, Skyward Sword art could be found in Lonlon Ranch, the Bombchu Shop in Hyrule Castle Town, and the Gerudo Fortress. It was a fun Easter Egg to discover back in 2011, especially since Skyward Sword was still months away, but these days it’s a bit of an odd inclusion.

Though never explicit, the composer ghosts guarding the Sun’s Song (and Link’s first ReDead encounter) have always been assumed to be inspired by Mario and Luigi. They are brothers; Flat is short, squat, and red; Sharp is lanky and green. They still appear in Ocarina of Time this way, which isn't surprising, since they are key characters you must meet to get a very useful song. Fans have also speculated that Talon and Ingo are Mario and Luigi-inspired for similar reasons, but it’s worth noting that they are not brothers.

Recent findings suggest that in the Spirit Temple there is a large statue of a woman and for reasons that have never been explained, Link could attach his hookshot to her breasts. It served no purpose. It didn’t help solve a puzzle. If anything, it was confusing. But we all tried it and there is no shame in admitting it! That was removed for the 3DS remake, and it remains removed in 2026.

This is a very subtle reference to Wind Waker/Breath of the Wild/Tears of the Kingdom and is potentially the only addition to the remake that looks toward the future of the Zelda franchise. Obviously, plenty of characters in Ocarina later appear in Majora’s Mask (another remake of that is hopefully being considered), but it would be inaccurate to call those intentional Easter Eggs.

Recent findings suggest that however, in Kokiri Forest and in the neighboring Lost Woods, the magical debris floating in the air often resembles a Korok as it would later appear in the series. It makes sense, too, because the Koroks are meant to be what the Kokiri transformed into following The Great Flood.

In a recent development, for more on the Ocarina of Time remake, you can find our review here. You can also find our interview with the game's producers here.

Cannabis addiction linked to 57% higher odds of suicidal thoughts

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (951 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As marijuana becomes more widely available and accepted, researchers are uncovering notable questions about its effects on mental health.
  • Sources indicate that published in the Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs, the research found that adults with cannabis use disorder had 57% higher odds of reporting suicidal thoughts compared with those without the condition.
  • The findings come from an analysis of more than 415,000 American adults who participated in the National Survey on Drug Use and Health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As marijuana becomes more widely available and accepted, researchers are uncovering notable questions about its effects on mental health. A major latest study suggests that people who struggle to control their cannabis use face a substantially greater likelihood of experiencing suicidal thoughts.

Sources indicate that published in the Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs, the research found that adults with cannabis use disorder had 57% higher odds of reporting suicidal thoughts compared with those without the condition. Despite major shifts in marijuana laws and public attitudes, this troubling association remained remarkably consistent over a decade.

The findings come from an analysis of more than 415,000 American adults who participated in the National Survey on Drug Use and Health. Researchers examined data collected between 2014 and 2023, a period when cannabis became increasingly accessible across the United States.

Recent findings suggest that "What surprised me most was not that cannabis use disorder was associated with suicidal thoughts, but that this association did not appear to strengthen over time," stated lead author Tosin Philip Oyetunji, MPH, a doctoral student in public health at the University of California, Merced. "[Yet,] it remains an key mental health concern that deserves attention.".

Cannabis and Suicidal Thoughts Show a Persistent Link.

It has been revealed that the connection between cannabis use disorder and suicidal thinking was observed across different age groups, sexes, and racial and ethnic backgrounds. However, women and younger adults indicated particularly elevated risks.

Importantly, the association remained even after researchers accounted for depression, psychological distress, and other factors that could influence mental health outcomes.

The consistency of the results was especially notable given how dramatically the cannabis landscape has changed. Recreational marijuana is now legal in half of U.S. states, and cannabis products have become increasingly potent. These developments have raised concerns among public health experts about whether broader access might contribute to worsening mental health.

Sources indicate that yet the study offers some reassurance on that particular question. Sidra Goldman-Mellor, PhD, a professor of public health at UC Merced and the study's senior author, noted that the association between cannabis use disorder and suicidal thoughts did not become stronger during the 10 years examined.

It has been revealed that "Suicidal ideation does not seem to have increased among people with cannabis use disorder, despite all this legal and social change," explained Goldman-Mellor. Yet, "people with cannabis use disorder are still at a very substantially increased likelihood of experiencing serious suicidal thoughts, and that's not something that is widely understood.".

Why Cannabis Use Disorder Matters.

The researchers stress that these findings should not be interpreted as evidence that everyone who uses marijuana faces the same elevated risk.

In a recent development, the study focused specifically on cannabis use disorder, a condition in which people have difficulty controlling their marijuana consumption even when it causes problems in their lives. Someone with the disorder may continue using cannabis despite harmful consequences or repeated attempts to cut back.

This distinction is important because problematic cannabis use differs from occasional or otherwise nonproblematic consumption.

It has been revealed that the findings also do not establish that cannabis use disorder directly causes suicidal thoughts. Because the research identified an association rather than a cause-and-effect relationship, it cannot determine whether problematic cannabis use contributes to suicidal thinking, whether underlying mental health difficulties contribute to both conditions, or whether other factors help explain the connection.

Nevertheless, the results point to a significant mental health concern that deserves greater recognition, particularly among people seeking help for problematic cannabis use.

Researchers Urge Greater Mental Health Screening.

One practical implication is that health care professionals should look beyond cannabis consumption itself when evaluating patients with cannabis use disorder.

Rather than focusing exclusively on depression or substance use symptoms, clinicians may benefit from asking patients directly about suicidal thoughts as part of a broader mental health assessment. This could help identify people who need additional care but whose struggles might otherwise remain unnoticed.

Recent findings suggest that "Someone seeking help for cannabis use disorder may also be experiencing suicidal thoughts that are not immediately apparent," said Oyetunji. "The goal is not to assume that everyone with cannabis use disorder is suicidal but to identify those who may need additional assessment, treatment, or support.".

The study arrives at a time when marijuana is increasingly viewed as a relatively low-risk substance. Public perceptions have shifted considerably, and negative attitudes toward cannabis have declined alongside expanding legalization and social acceptance.

However, these changes have not eliminated the mental health challenges associated with cannabis use disorder. Even though the strength of the association with suicidal thoughts did not increase over the study period, the elevated odds remained substantial.

The researchers suggest that health care providers, policymakers, and community organizations can play an important role by improving awareness, identifying vulnerable individuals, and making appropriate mental health support more accessible.

As attitudes toward marijuana continue to evolve, the findings serve as a reminder that the needs of people experiencing problematic cannabis use should remain a public health priority.

Noted Oyetunji, "As cannabis becomes more accessible and socially accepted, we should ensure that the people struggling with its use are not overlooked.".

The Switch 2 Pro Controller Can Make Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Even Better

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (769 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time hit Switch 2 today, and, as Kyle Hilliard pointed out in our review, it is pretty excellent.
  • After hours of running around, I was awestruck by the level of detail and updates, but I found myself constantly fighting with the camera, or at the very least, needing to take a strange claw-style grip to be able to direct the camera with the right stick, while holding down the A button to sprint.
  • If you, like me, struggle to comfortably steer the fresh free camera while running through hallways, towns, dungeons, and, yes, Hyrule Field, you might want to consider remapping your controller.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time hit Switch 2 today, and, as Kyle Hilliard pointed out in our review, it is pretty excellent. Along with its remarkable visual upgrade, the latest Switch 2 remake of Ocarina of Time adds quality-of-life improvements and modernizes the control scheme. As part of that, Nintendo has added the ability to jump and sprint. While that works well to make the game feel new, I promptly realized it sometimes clashes with another new improvement: a free camera controlled by the right stick. Holding down the sprint button to get through areas as fast as possible can make it tricky to keep the camera where you want it, but thankfully, if you have the Switch 2 Pro Controller, there's an easy fix.

After hours of running around, I was awestruck by the level of detail and updates, but I found myself constantly fighting with the camera, or at the very least, needing to take a strange claw-style grip to be able to direct the camera with the right stick, while holding down the A button to sprint. If you're a casual Switch 2 player, you might not have even noticed the back buttons on the Pro Controller, or you just have no idea what they do. Those buttons can be remapped on a per-game basis and it's a simple process. Everyone has their own preferences, but, for example, for high-mobility shooters, I like remapping one of those to reload and one to jump. I've never felt the need to remap in a Zelda game, but after feeling the need to do so with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, I might do so going forward.

If you, like me, struggle to comfortably steer the fresh free camera while running through hallways, towns, dungeons, and, yes, Hyrule Field, you might want to consider remapping your controller. As you can see in the above image, the placement of Jump and Dash on the face buttons can make it difficult to simultaneously control the camera and sprint. This isn't typically a problem in most modern games, as clicking the right stick is often a toggle to sprint, but in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2, you need to hold the button.

If you have the Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller, copying one button's functionality to the buttons on the back of the controller is simple. All you need to do is hold the Home button on the Switch 2 Pro Controller for a moment until the Switch 2 system menu appears on the right side. Along with Power Options and any Bluetooth audio devices you have available, there is also the option to map GL and GR, the controller's back buttons on the left and right, respectively.

Navigate down the menu to the GL and GR, then select which one you'd like to map. It will ask you which button you want to assign to the one you selected. Everyone can choose whatever makes sense in their own head, but mapping A (Roll and Dash) to GL and X (Jump) to GR made the most sense to me. Now, while I'm using the Switch 2 Pro Controller, I can use my middle finger to hold the GL button to Dash around without removing my thumb from the camera-controlling right stick.

Recent findings suggest that and the best part is that, since you're not removing the functionality of the A or X buttons, you can still use them when it makes sense. For example, A also controls actions like opening up a treasure chest or door, and in my head, that feels like a face-button action, whereas rolling and dashing feel right mapped to the back buttons. The only downside is that, since this functionality is upcoming for Switch 2 Pro Controllers, it isn't available if you're using the Joy-Cons or a Switch 1 Pro Controller. Also, it can make switching over to handheld mode challenging, as you don't have access to the back buttons in that play style.

Sources indicate that even if you don't have the ability to take advantage of this tip, either because you don't own a Switch 2 Pro Controller or because you prefer playing in handheld mode, you should still absolutely play the Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. To learn more about the experience and why it's a must-play, head to our review.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Years ago, I had this dream where I was parkouring through a greatly sunken version of Venice, no doubt sourced from the many hours I put into Assassin's Creed 2 as a teen who should have been studying for their GCSEs a lot more than they were. It's stuck with me after all this time mostly because of how much I wanted to capture that feeling again somehow, as the real Assassin's Creed didn't quite cut it. And lo and behold, there I was today browsing Bluesky when I came across Boars in Rome, a Mirror's Edge and Counter Strike Surf inspired parkour platformer set in a dystopian version of Rome.

Truthfully, witnessing the clip I've shared below was baffling to me. "This is what I dreamt of!" More or less, anyway, for the setting isn't quite the same; "You have been selected to start a newly introduced life off planet. Earth has been abandoned," explains the game's Steam page. "Machines keep working and nature claims what remains. Find out what happened while you were frozen in time by exploring the remnants of Rome where historical monuments mix with futurist megastructures.".

According to recent reports, mirrors Edge x Counter Strike Surf where you parkour on anything! Be smooth n stylish in dystopian Rome. Or just jump around and explore, whatever works for you. It's called Boars in Rome! #PitchYaGame[image or embed].

Not all of it matches that dream of mine, some of it leans much more into brutalism than the typical, much older architecture you'd expect of Rome, but it's there nonetheless. In motion, Boars in Rome feels quite oneiric too. There is so much more control over the game's avatar than what my real body is capable of, or wants to do. You can run, jump, slide and wallrun, positioning it quite closely to VHOLUME mechanically. Where it differs is in its additives, movement tech like being able to swing on lampposts or vault over low down obstacles.

VHOLUME is more of a game about providing you with a simple toolkit and leaving you to push it to its maximum. Boars in Roam is a touch more expressive, and I'd dare to even call it an immersive sim. The levels you can romp around are linear, you have an end point to reach, only the journey is up to you. It certainly feels appropriate to put it in the im sim camp given that, at least the game's first level, calls to mind Viktor Antonov's work on Dishonored (and Half-Life 2, too, honestly).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content.
  • As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content.
  • Recent findings suggest that the first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the newly introduced maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content. Now, the developer has revealed how it plans to use some of that time, and the first port of call is Battlefield Labs.

As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content. This includes Season 2, of course, and a big component of what it’s bringing to the game is headed to Labs.

Recent findings suggest that the first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the newly introduced maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2. BF Studios claims the map falls between Eastwood and Mirak Valley, in terms of size.

According to recent reports, the blog post even likened it to Battlefield 1’s St. Quentin Scar, and Battlefield 5’s Arras. Although we’ve yet to actually play it, the size and description do sound really well, especially in a game as starved of substantial maps as Battlefield 6 at the moment is.

According to recent reports, another thing BF Studios wants to test is the way ground vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, which is pretty standard for most Battlefield maps. Interestingly, there appears to be some sort of mechanic unique to Contaminated that the developer also wants to evaluate.

More Labs sessions are planned, including one that will show off newly introduced gameplay tools and vehicles. The AH-6 Little Bird helicopter was specifically namedropped, which makes sense given that it’s going to be part of Season 2’s content.

Industry observers note that battlefield Labs sessions will also extend beyond the biggest-ticket items of maps and vehicles. BF Studios said we should expect tests of upcoming features, like the Aircraft Radar, as part of a list of other air combat updates.

According to recent reports, ground vehicles, and they way the various rockets interact with them, will also be evaluated in a different session, with specific adjustments planned for RPGs and TOWs. And, of course, the work to improve and perfect hit reg remains ongoing, and future tweaks will go through Labs first.

There’s even more exciting news for fans of major maps, as the blog post also confirmed that Battlefield 4’s Golmud Railway is right now in the works, planned to go live in a future season. Golmud Railway will show up early in Labs, and you can expect it to evolve over multiple sessions.

In a recent development, for context, when it does arrive in Battlefield 6, Golmud Railway will be the largest map in the game, which is saying something. Though the map is beloved by vehicle players, it has its challenges elsewhere, and BF Studios indicates it will be looking at all that when it creates the BF6, emphasising that it won’t be a simple port of the BF4 original.

Finally, the post throws a bone to Redsec battle royale players still waiting for a Solo mode. BF Studios continues to test the idea internally, but it’s taking a while. Needless to say, there are so many aspects that need to be considered. Game pace, balance, player survivability, match flow just to name a few.

In a recent development, redsec BR was built with squads in mind, so that task is extra challenging. Though the developer didn’t say when we can expect Solos to arrive in Labs, players will get a chance to experience it before it enters the live game.

10 Changes You Might Not Have Noticed in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1358 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is pretty amazing.
  • These are just some of the big changes, however, as Nintendo made a lot more changes, and some of them you might not even have noticed since they are so small.
  • In a recent development, this is a very small change that you might not have realized was made between the original game and the remake, and that is that the merchants actually move.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake is pretty amazing. The team didn’t mess around, and instead changed many aspects of this beloved Nintendo 64 title. It has updated graphics, slightly altered story beats, and more. Of course, since the team rebuilt Hyrule, that means they could make a few changes. Castle Town is now much more detailed, and even Death Mountain’s layout changed slightly.

These are just some of the big changes, however, as Nintendo made a lot more changes, and some of them you might not even have noticed since they are so small. Despite being small, these changes are just as notable as the large ones, as they make the game feel more complete.

In a recent development, this is a very small change that you might not have realized was made between the original game and the remake, and that is that the merchants actually move. While some of the shop owners had animation before, they typically just looked at Link.

Recent findings suggest that while playing the remake, you will see that each merchant is now far more animated, but the major difference is that they will actually turn their head to look at the item you are buying from them. While this change wasn’t needed, it definitely makes the shop owners feel more alive rather than watching them stand there.

Have you ever been to Castle Town at night in the original Ocarina of Time? No? Well, that is because you can’t go there at night. The drawbridge closes, preventing you from accessing the town after sunset. Luckily, you have the Sun Song to quickly change night into day, allowing you to enter the town.

This isn’t an matter, however, in the remake, as the town is constantly open to you. You can come and go as you please at any time of the day or night without anyone getting upset with you. You may have had it in your mind to keep going during the day, or maybe you just assumed that the gate was open and forgot that it closed in the original.

Fairy Thoughts didn’t exist in the original game. Instead, they are something new that is specific to the Ocarina of Time Remake. These small glowing symbols can be found on various surfaces around Hyrule, even in dungeons. Sometimes Fairy Thoughts act as hints to help you progress through the game, and other times they are small puzzles that fully restore Link’s health once they are solved.

Recent findings suggest that they are a neat little change that you might not have noticed while exploring, as they can be easy to overlook. I didn’t notice them for a long time, and since I found one, I have been going around looking for more.

You may have seen various little whirlwinds around Hyrule in the remake. These are used to summon the scarecrow, and they didn’t appear in the original. In the original Ocarina of Time, if you wanted to summon Pierre, you needed to find a spot where Navi would glow green instead of the normal blue. This indicated that it was a spot where the scarecrow song could be played.

In a recent development, now, if you want to summon Pierre the Wandering Scarecrow, you simply need to find a place where “the straw swirls in the wind.” Which is any location with a bit of swirling wind. At least these locations are easier to find.

There are some who received the Giant’s Knife from Goron City back in the day, swung it around to test it, and then ultimately got disappointed when it broke before they even left the area and got to test it on some enemies. For those who don’t know, this weapon is very fragile, making it so it breaks after just eight hits. It is a cautionary tale that teaches everyone that nothing is permanent, except the Master Sword.

Sources indicate that anyway, the weapon still breaks in the remake, but there has been a change. Nintendo removed the hitboxes from walls, so you can swing the weapon around and not have it break off the environment. Instead, it will break from striking enemies, as was intended.

The Biggoron Sword is quite powerful, and in the original game, many replaced the Master Sword with it because it could be swung at the same pace and it hit harder. The only difference was you couldn’t use your shield while wielding it. Despite that drawback, the Biggoron Sword was worth holding onto, as an experienced swordfighter didn’t need to worry about using their shield for the most part.

In a recent development, this sword has been changed in the remake. It is still massive, and requires both hands to swing. However, the swing speed of it is noticeably slower, making it more difficult to hit some enemies with the blade. This put more emphasis on the use of the Master Sword in certain situations.

Since The Ocarina of Time is a third-person title, you might not have realized that there was a first-person option in the original. The game did go into first-person when shooting your slingtshot, but otherwise, you needed to press a button for it, and even then it was temporary.

Sources indicate that the remake of the beloved title doesn’t even give you the option to go into first-person mode. Instead, it keeps you tied to the third-person camera. This is a bit of a strange change from the original and one that some people discovered right away, as they used to use first-person mode to get a closer look at the environment. To replace it, many have said that Nintendo should have added a photo mode.

Recent findings suggest that one of the side quests you can complete in Ocarina of Time is the one for the Happy Mask Salesman. This quest requires you to purchase various masks and sell them to citizens of Hyrule. However, in the original, you weren’t allowed to wear the masks as an adult. People always thought this was a bit strange, but it is a detail that didn’t matter much.

Industry observers note that the remake, on the other hand, allows you to wear the various masks as an adult. There isn’t anything special about wearing the masks as an adult versus wearing them as a kid, but it is an interesting little detail that Nintendo added that wasn’t in the original game.

Recent findings suggest that after progressing through the game, you finally make your way to the Spirit Temple. This is one of my personal favorite temples in the game, and like the other temples in the game, it has undergone some changes in the remake.

Sources indicate that one of the more peculiar changes is the one made to the large Gerudo statue in the temple. In the original, certain parts of the statue were able to be grappled using your hookshot, but there were never any obvious grapple points. This has been changed in the remake, with the statue still being there, but the grapple points are now gone, so you can no longer grab the statue if it’s something that interests you.

It has been revealed that this is a bit of an odd change, but one that people are thankful has been made. In the original Ocarina of Time, when you reach the Zora’s Domain, you talk to King Zora, and you eventually get him to scoot out of the way so you can visit Lord Jabu-Jabu. This scoot is obnoxiously long, as King Zora likes to take his time getting out of your way.

It has been revealed that well, in the remake, King Zora still scoots out of the way, but the change is that Nintendo made is significantly quicker. When timed, King Zora moves out of the way roughly eight seconds faster than he does in the original Ocarina of Time. Thankfully, we only need to wait around 20 seconds now instead of almost 30. Nintendo kept this hilarious if frustrating part of the title in, but streamlined it considerably.

#40385. Tiny magnets deep inside the brain could transform Parkinson’s treatment

Tiny magnets deep inside the brain could transform Parkinson’s treatment

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1178 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An international research team has developed a new technique that uses magnetic fields and tiny particles to stimulate regions deep inside the brain, potentially opening the door to a less invasive treatment for Parkinson's disease.
  • The technique involves injecting specially designed magnetic nanoplatelets into a targeted area of the brain.
  • Why Parkinson's Treatment Often Requires Brain Implants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An international research team has developed a new technique that uses magnetic fields and tiny particles to stimulate regions deep inside the brain, potentially opening the door to a less invasive treatment for Parkinson's disease. In experiments involving mice with Parkinson's-like symptoms, the approach significantly improved movement problems without requiring permanently implanted electrodes.

The technique involves injecting specially designed magnetic nanoplatelets into a targeted area of the brain. When exposed to an external magnetic field, these particles generate tiny forces that activate nearby nerve cells. Unlike conventional brain stimulation treatments, which rely on surgically implanted electrodes, the latest approach uses magnetic forces to influence brain activity. The findings, published in Advanced Science, come from researchers at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU), RWTH Aachen, and the Universities of Maastricht (the Netherlands) and Leuven (Belgium).

Why Parkinson's Treatment Often Requires Brain Implants.

According to recent reports, parkinson's disease develops as brain cells responsible for producing dopamine gradually break down. Dopamine is a chemical messenger that plays a vital role in controlling movement. As its levels decline, communication within the brain's movement circuits becomes disrupted, contributing to tremors and other motor difficulties.

Recent findings suggest that for some patients, deep brain stimulation can help control these symptoms. This treatment uses a device known as a brain pacemaker, which is implanted beneath the collarbone and connected to electrodes placed deep inside the brain. The electrodes deliver electrical stimulation to a region called the subthalamic nucleus (STN for short), helping to modify abnormal activity in the brain circuits responsible for movement.

Although this treatment can provide substantial relief, it requires a complex surgical procedure and does not work for everyone.

"The procedure is relatively complex, however, and not always successful," explains Prof. Dr. Danijela Gregurec from the Department of Chemistry and Pharmacy at FAU. "This puts many Parkinson's patients off, and not all patients are suitable candidates for one of these pacemakers.".

The researchers believe magnetic stimulation could eventually provide another option, allowing doctors to influence the same deep brain structures without leaving electrodes permanently implanted.

How Tiny Magnetic Particles Stimulate Brain Cells.

The new technology takes advantage of the ability of certain nerve cells to detect physical pressure and mechanical forces.

"We use magnetic nanoparticles that we implant in the brain," Gregurec explains. "They have a special shape and a magnetic structure. They were developed in order to transform magnetic fields into tiny mechanical forces.".

Rather than sending electrical pulses directly into the brain, the technique uses these particles to produce extremely small physical movements when a magnetic field is applied.

"The traditional method establishes an electrical connection to the brain," she says. "In contrast, we use the neurons' natural mechanosensors to influence regions deep within the brain.".

The process works by gently changing the shape of nearby nerve cell membranes. Imagine pressing a finger against an inflated balloon and creating a small indentation in its surface. The magnetic particles produce a similar effect on a microscopic scale.

This slight deformation opens specialized channels in the cell membrane that respond to mechanical pressure. Once opened, these channels allow electrically charged particles called ions to enter the nerve cells, changing their electrical activity and providing a way to stimulate the targeted brain circuits.

Magnetic Brain Stimulation Improves Movement in Mice.

Sources indicate that to investigate whether the technology could relieve Parkinson's symptoms, the international research team conducted experiments using mice with damage to the same types of dopamine-producing nerve cells affected by the disease in humans. This damage caused movement difficulties resembling those seen in Parkinson's patients.

In a recent development, "Together with our partners from Maastricht, we injected magnetic nanoparticles developed here at FAU into the animals' subthalamic nucleus," Gregurec explains. "That is the very region in the brain that is also an important target for conventional deep brain stimulation in Parkinson's disease.".

The researchers used precise stereotactic injection techniques to deliver the particles to the intended location. These methods rely on carefully calculated three-dimensional coordinates to guide instruments into specific brain structures. Accurate placement was particularly crucial because the treatment needed to affect the correct neural circuits involved in movement.

Industry observers note that after the particles were positioned, the researchers applied an external magnetic field. The results were encouraging: the mice demonstrated significant improvements in their movement deficits.

"The effect is roughly equivalent to what we would have expected after implanting a brain pacemaker," indicates Gregurec.

The findings suggest that magnetic nanoparticles could provide a different way to achieve some of the benefits of conventional deep brain stimulation, without the need for permanently implanted electrodes.

Could Future Parkinson's Treatments Use Magnetic Headbands?

Another encouraging finding involved how the brain responded to the implanted particles over time. The magnetic nanoparticles remained in place throughout an observation period lasting several months, and the researchers found no signs of inflammation. This suggests that the particles were well tolerated during the experiments.

Industry observers note that however, delivering the particles still required an injection directly into the brain. Gregurec and her colleagues are now investigating ways to make the procedure even less invasive.

Recent findings suggest that one possibility is to develop particles that could be injected into the bloodstream and then travel into the brain by crossing the blood-brain barrier. This protective boundary normally prevents many substances circulating in the blood from entering brain tissue. Finding a way to deliver the particles across it could eliminate the need for direct brain injections.

The researchers are also exploring compact wearable devices capable of generating the magnetic fields needed for stimulation. One possibility is a headband that patients could put on themselves, potentially making treatment more convenient and adjustable.

These ideas remain at an early stage, and the researchers expect that several more years of development will be needed before the technology could be considered for clinical use.

In a recent development, "Nevertheless, we are convinced that the new method has enormous potential," Gregurec states. "It is not only considerably simpler and cheaper than a conventional brain pacemaker, it is probably also more flexible. Adjusting the parameters of the magnetic field would allow us to control the nanoparticles more accurately.".

In a recent development, beyond its potential medical applications, the technology could also become a valuable scientific tool. By allowing researchers to stimulate nerve cells through carefully controlled mechanical forces, it offers a upcoming way to explore how physical changes at the cellular level influence brain activity.

Although the treatment has so far been demonstrated only in animals, its ability to improve movement without permanently implanted electrodes represents a promising step toward newly introduced approaches to Parkinson's disease and brain stimulation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sundays are for waking up covered in sand. The roof of your house is missing. A small man stands in the emptied bed of a dump truck. "You know, everybody's always asking about Elder Scrolls 6," he says. "You know, everybody's always asking about Elder Scrolls 6," he repeats. "Things first went awry when I turned up for my appointment to find a tall German man wearing a cowboy hat asking a PR if he could play the game," you blurt out. The posterior momentarily stops moving towards you. Buoyed, you continue to tell a story you heard from VGC's Chris Scullion.

I was asked if I minded sharing my one-to-one appointment with this chap too, to which my inherent British cowardly courtesy kicked in and I lied that it was perfectly fine.

Recent findings suggest that "I want drums", he noted as he entered the room. "We are playing Dani California by Red Hot Chili Peppers." Rather than ask him whether he also fancied telling me where I was going for dinner later, I picked up my guitar and went along with it, eager to just play the game.

The bottom begins its agonising crawl towards your kisser once more. You can feel the occupants of parliamentary benches begin to sense a disturbance in the force. Maybe if you can make the bumholder sad, that'll do the trick. You try to remember how Sebastian Cardoso of Game Studio Unlocked's presentation on the tragic fates of game studios after acquisitions went.

Sources indicate that A hundred and twenty-three of the 362 developers were shut outright. The average life from acquisition to closure is 6.4 years and the median is 5, meaning half of all closed studios were dead within five years of their acquisition.

The familiar names mostly died fast. EA closed Pandemic two years after buying it. Sony shut Firewalk barely a year and a half in. Warner Bros. closed Player First roughly seven months after acquiring it. Bluepoint, closed at the five-year mark, is exactly what the median looks like.

It's no use. That arse's shadow its creeping across ever more of your face like your're a planet with a nose and it's the Vogon Constructor Fleet. Maybe you can somehow contort your head to the side. Arrrggghh. You call on all the strength of muscles you barely ever use and think of the incredible gymnastic feats executed by Physical Contortion Gamer's Josh Wolens during an ongoing GTA diary series.

Attempting to do flips, then, just sort of rotates your entire body below the diaphragm while your head and chest area remain bolt upright, rigid in such a way that you could feasibly fly a flag from your own thorax.

It has been revealed that which looks odd. Nevertheless, it is pretty fun to scoot and roll your way through Los Santos. At one point, I attempted a double frontflip in the middle of a part of the map that had been deleted for some reason. It didn't quite work out, and I ended up colliding with and possibly killing a man in a fursuit.

It has been revealed that it doesn't work. You can't get away. You begin to scream. The posterioperator stops repeating the words "You know, everybody's always asking about Elder Scrolls 6". Instead, he asks where that mysterious German cowboy you mentioned earlier has gone. You don't have a clue, and can't help admitting as much. "Ah well." The derriere resumes its descent, now mere inches from your mug. This is the end. You have one last rummage through your mind for possible solutions.

It has been revealed that respec's Tom Orry hasn't managed to save you. "Fine, sit on my face and send me to hell," you shout into the pinkish ring of doom as British cops prepare to ram-raid your abode and arrest you for crimes against a prude's definition of acceptable shagging.

It has been revealed that the bum stops. Its owner asks if you've just said the word Sentinel. "Yes," you lie.

It has been revealed that the arse is raised and swapped for the face of a man. "What a perfect time for you to realise what The Elder Scrolls 6 is actually called," he notes.

You notice he's not Todd Howard. Or Adrian Edmondson.

It has been revealed that "It's Ade's month off and they needed another baldy to play this esteemed role," Sir Patrick Stewart confirms, clearly responding the look of befuddlement your face can still have since it hasn't been crushed by a ten-tonne tush. You wonder how you didn't recognise his voice before, especially given he played the emperor in Oblivion.

"Here's to the next Bethesda game after Starfield," the Stew sings as the police bust through the door and he's beamed up before they can tackle him.

In a recent development, we’re expecting a content upgrade each month, with the majority of the biggest additions happening on the game’s existing maps. There is, however, at least one new map in the works, but it won’t be here until sometime in April.

January’s chapter is titled Headwinds, kicking off on January 27. This segment will see the addition of a latest matchmaking option for players above level 40 - at or near the game’s endgame. We’re also expecting a new Map Condition, and a new Player Project for everyone to contribute to.

Things start getting interesting in February, when Shrouded Sky will begin. This chapter brings three exciting additions to Arc Raiders. There will be a new Map Condition, new Arc Threat, and the start of another Player Project.

Interestingly, we’re going to see some sort of map patch during the month, but Embark didn’t share anymore details. The next Raider Deck will also deploy in February, alongside a newly introduced Expedition Window.

In a recent development, the Flashpoint chapter begins in March, when we’re expecting another new Map Condition, one more new Arc Threat, as well as another Player Project. March’s most interesting addition is an patch to everyone’s trusty rooster friend, Scrappy.

Industry observers note that finally, April is when the major guns come out, because that’s when the first new map of 2026 will arrive in Arc Raiders. With it, comes a new large Arc, which is to be expected. A new Map Condition will debut then, too, likely starting off on the new map.

That’s pretty much it, but seeing as we’re just one day away from the start of the January stage, things are about to get exciting again in Arc Raiders.

Ozempic and Mounjaro may have a surprising effect on your brain

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that popular medications used to treat obesity and type 2 diabetes, including semaglutide and tirzepatide, may have effects that extend beyond weight loss and blood sugar control.
  • To examine this possibility, researchers from the University of Gothenburg and the University of Copenhagen reviewed the existing scientific evidence at the invitation of the journal Science.
  • Recent findings suggest that studies involving animals suggest that GLP-1 medications can influence learning and memory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that popular medications used to treat obesity and type 2 diabetes, including semaglutide and tirzepatide, may have effects that extend beyond weight loss and blood sugar control. These drugs also influence biological processes involved in brain function, raising questions about whether they could help preserve memory and thinking abilities.

To examine this possibility, researchers from the University of Gothenburg and the University of Copenhagen reviewed the existing scientific evidence at the invitation of the journal Science.

Recent findings suggest that studies involving animals suggest that GLP-1 medications can influence learning and memory. However, research involving humans has produced less consistent findings. Analyses of patient health records have found an association between GLP-1 treatment and a reduced risk of dementia among people with type 2 diabetes. These observational findings are encouraging, but they cannot determine whether the medications themselves are responsible for the lower risk.

More definitive results have also raised questions. In Novo Nordisk's EVOKE and EVOKE+ clinical trials, semaglutide failed to slow the progression of early Alzheimer's disease. Although the treatment affected several biological markers associated with Alzheimer's, those changes did not translate into a measurable slowing of the disease.

Why Weight Loss Drugs May Still Benefit the Brain.

Despite the disappointing Alzheimer's results, researchers believe GLP-1 medications could still offer cognitive benefits to certain groups of patients.

According to recent reports, people living with obesity or type 2 diabetes sometimes experience difficulties with attention, planning, and the speed at which they process information. These cognitive problems are often associated with metabolic health and blood vessel function, suggesting they may respond differently to treatment than the changes caused by Alzheimer's disease.

Improving blood sugar regulation, metabolism, or vascular health could potentially help preserve cognitive abilities, even if the same medications cannot slow an established neurodegenerative disease.

Stina Börchers, the review's first author and a researcher affiliated with both the University of Gothenburg and the University of Copenhagen, emphasizes the need to determine whether starting treatment earlier could make a difference.

Industry observers note that "We need to find out whether these treatments can help people with obesity or diabetes preserve their cognitive abilities, particularly if treatment begins before cognitive problems become established. It is also notable to identify which patients might benefit," says Stina Börchers.

Unlocking Upcoming Treatments to Protect Memory.

It has been revealed that A central unanswered question is how GLP-1 medications might influence the brain. Their potential cognitive effects could result from improvements in metabolic health, direct actions within the brain, or a combination of both.

Understanding these mechanisms could help researchers identify which patients are most likely to benefit and potentially lead to medications designed specifically to support memory and other thinking abilities.

Christoffer Clemmensen, the review's senior author and a research group leader at the University of Copenhagen, sees an opportunity to use increasingly advanced obesity treatments to explore the connection between metabolism and the brain.

Sources indicate that "Obesity medicines are becoming increasingly sophisticated, offering new opportunities to understand how metabolic regulation influences brain function. By disentangling the direct and indirect effects of these drugs on the brain, we may ultimately be able to develop treatments specifically aimed at preserving cognitive function," says Christoffer Clemmensen.

The researchers are calling for clinical trials that evaluate memory, attention, and other cognitive abilities beginning when patients first start treatment. Following these changes over time could help establish whether GLP-1 drugs genuinely protect brain function and clarify who might benefit most.

They also stress that treatment is not without potential drawbacks, particularly for older adults and people who are physically frail. Rapid weight loss can lead to a reduction in muscle mass, which may weaken physical function and offset some of the possible benefits.

Careful monitoring will therefore be essential as researchers investigate whether today's weight loss and diabetes medications could eventually provide latest ways to protect the brain.

Materials provided by University of Gothenburg. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
